articles.title: Trump, Xi and Putin issue joint declaration after first three-way meeting
articles.summary:
Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin met for about 90 minutes on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen on Thursday evening and released a joint statement, the ABC reported. According to AAP and the ABC, it commits the three to UN reform, higher oil product supply and lower nuclear risk, and says bodies such as the International Criminal Court should not abuse their jurisdiction.

The statement does not mention the wars in Ukraine or Iran, the ABC and AAP said. Trump said Ukraine was discussed. Xi described the talks as constructive, AAP reported. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk criticised the meeting in a social media post.
keyFacts: Meeting lasted about 90 minutes in Shenzhen
Statement covers UN reform, oil supply and nuclear risk
Text does not mention Ukraine or Iran

articles.title: Putin rules out partial truce and vows response to Crimean Bridge strikes
articles.summary:
Russian President Vladimir Putin said after his talks with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping that Russia would not make agreements following Ukraine's strikes on the Crimean Bridge, according to TASS as reported by the Kyiv Post. He said Moscow's response would be more painful than the damage to the bridge, IBTimes reported.

Putin said he had asked Russia's Security Council to reconsider a possible halt to strikes on energy and maritime targets. Ukraine's defence ministry said Neptune missiles hit the bridge's rail section, the third strike in a week. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin said some sections could reopen within one to two months.
keyFacts: Bridge struck three times in a week
Putin dropped a possible energy and maritime truce
Some sections may reopen in one to two months

articles.title: Second COP31 draft drops fossil fuel transition and adaptation finance figure
articles.summary:
A revised draft of the main COP31 decision released in Antalya on Thursday no longer refers to transitioning away from fossil fuels, AAP and Climate Home News reported. The text was cut from 18 pages to nine and also removed a proposed adaptation finance figure of at least $US120 billion a year by 2035 and a reference to the Pacific Resilience Facility, AAP said.

The draft keeps targets to raise electricity to 35 per cent of final energy use by 2035 and to triple renewable capacity. Chris Bowen, the COP31 president of negotiations, said it used the strongest terms likely to win approval. Environment groups including Greenpeace and the Australian Conservation Foundation criticised the changes.
keyFacts: Draft halved from 18 to nine pages
Fossil fuel transition wording removed
35 per cent electrification target retained

articles.title: Anthropic shares open 34 per cent above IPO price in Nasdaq debut
articles.summary:
Anthropic shares opened at $US111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, about 34 per cent above the $US83 IPO price, according to Forbes and AAP. AAP said the company's market value briefly reached about $US2.1 trillion. The shares later eased and were up about 19 per cent at $US98.56 in early afternoon trade, AP reported.

Anthropic sold 980 million shares, raising about $US81.3 billion, which Forbes said is the largest IPO on record. Chief executive Dario Amodei told CNBC the company hoped to become investment grade, AAP reported. One fund manager quoted by AAP said the company needed to reach profitability soon.
keyFacts: Opened at $US111.50 versus $US83 IPO price
IPO raised about $US81.3 billion
Trades under the ticker ANT

articles.title: Wall Street falls as S&P 500 heads for sixth straight loss
articles.summary:
US shares fell on Thursday despite Anthropic's debut, with the S&P 500 down 1.1 per cent in early afternoon trade after an early gain of 1.3 per cent, AP reported. The Dow Jones index was down 766 points, or 1.5 per cent, and the Nasdaq was down 1 per cent at 12.45pm New York time, AP said.

Nvidia reversed an early gain of 4.7 per cent to trade lower, and Micron and CoreWeave also turned down, according to AP. Williams-Sonoma fell 13.9 per cent. The US 10-year Treasury yield eased to 5.06 per cent. Benzinga reported the S&P 500 was on track for a sixth consecutive daily loss.
keyFacts: S&P 500 down 1.1 per cent in afternoon trade
Dow down 766 points at 12.45pm ET
10-year Treasury yield at 5.06 per cent

articles.title: Israel says it has ended tank raid in central Gaza
articles.summary:
Israel's military said on Thursday it had concluded a tank raid in central Gaza aimed at destroying a suspected Hamas tunnel, Reuters reported. Reuters described it as the most prominent ground incursion across the ceasefire's yellow line since the October 2025 truce. The military said the main Salahudeen road had reopened.

Residents told Reuters sporadic gunfire could still be heard and the road remained dangerous. The Hamas-run Gaza media office said about 6,000 people fled the area on Wednesday. Gaza health authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli strikes since the ceasefire, while Israel's military says five soldiers have been killed in that time.
keyFacts: Raid targeted a suspected Hamas tunnel
About 6,000 people fled, Gaza media office said
Salahudeen road reopened, military said

articles.title: Riyadh tower housing Saudi wealth fund damaged during Houthi missile attack
articles.summary:
The Public Investment Fund tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District was damaged on Thursday, Reuters reported citing three sources, according to The National. The Saudi-led coalition said it dealt with a missile threat towards Riyadh and that falling debris caused material damage. It did not say whether the missile was intercepted.

The coalition said it also destroyed a cruise missile, intercepted four ballistic missiles and destroyed a launch platform in Yemen's Saada province, The National reported. Gulf News said the building is 80 storeys tall. The extent of damage and any casualties were not immediately known.
keyFacts: Tower is in the King Abdullah Financial District
Coalition blamed falling debris for damage
Casualties not immediately known

articles.title: Pentagon official leaves Ukraine meeting after criticising Kyiv's long-range strikes
articles.summary:
US Under Secretary for Policy Elbridge Colby told a Ukraine Defence Contact Group meeting in Brussels that Ukraine's long-range strikes on Russia had little military value, then left before a classified Ukrainian briefing, the Kyiv Post reported, citing The Telegraph.

German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius reportedly called the remarks "stupid", according to the Kyiv Post and The Independent. British Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the strikes had degraded Russia's war capacity. Britain pledged 1,000 long-range drones to Ukraine, the Kyiv Post said. The Pentagon's account of the meeting was not included in the reports.
keyFacts: Meeting was held in Brussels
Colby left before a Ukrainian briefing
Britain pledged 1,000 long-range drones

articles.title: Israeli ambassador says Israel will respond to Australia's settler sanctions
articles.summary:
Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, said Israel would respond to Australia's new sanctions over West Bank settlement activity, AAP reported. He described the move as megaphone diplomacy. An Israeli government spokesman said responses were being considered and would be announced at the appropriate time.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong on Wednesday sanctioned three people and four organisations, including for the first time a construction company and its owner, AAP said. Settler leader Daniela Weiss and her organisation Nachala were also listed. A DFAT spokesperson said the measures support a two-state solution.
keyFacts: Sanctions cover three people and four organisations
A construction firm was listed for the first time
Israel has not said what its response will be

articles.title: Greens accuse Victorian Labor over how-to-vote cards putting Greens first
articles.summary:
Victorian Labor volunteers handed out how-to-vote cards at early voting centres that list the Greens first and Labor second, AAP reported. In Point Cook and Tarneit, where the Greens are running open tickets, the cards leave the rest of the ballot blank. The Greens say the cards are designed to mislead voters.

Premier Ben Carroll did not directly explain the cards and told voters to put Labor first, AAP said. Point Cook MP Mathew Hilakari defended them. Transparency International Australia said Victoria has no truth-in-advertising law for campaigns. The ABC separately reported an independent's card in Prahran closely resembles the Greens design.
keyFacts: Cards authorised by Labor state secretary Steve Staikos
Issue raised in Point Cook and Tarneit
State election is on November 28

articles.title: VEC isolates about 700 early votes after unauthorised person worked at Richmond centre
articles.summary:
The Victorian Electoral Commission isolated sealed boxes holding about 700 votes after an unauthorised person gained access to the Richmond early voting centre on the first day of early voting, AAP and news.com.au's News24 reported. AAP said the person had posed as a VEC casual worker.

Electoral Commissioner Sven Bluemmel said the integrity of the vote had not been compromised, according to AAP. The VEC has not said publicly what will happen to the isolated ballots. Early voting continues ahead of the November 28 state election.
keyFacts: About 700 votes isolated in sealed boxes
Incident happened on first day of early voting
Commissioner says integrity not compromised

articles.title: Productivity Commission proposes cutting business non-financial reporting
articles.summary:
A Productivity Commission interim report requested by Treasurer Jim Chalmers recommends winding back some non-financial reporting rules for businesses, AAP reported. It says mandatory climate-risk reporting should not be extended to medium-sized companies with revenue of $50 million or more from 2027.

The report also says some emissions reporting imposes unnecessarily high costs and that employers performing well on gender equality could report less often, AAP said. Commissioner Angela Jackson said reporting adds to a large regulatory load. The commission is also considering removing six-monthly payment-time reporting for small suppliers. Its final report is due by February.
keyFacts: Interim report released on Friday
Climate reporting extension to mid-sized firms opposed
Final report due by February

articles.title: Unemployment rises to 4.9 per cent as employment falls by 43,500 in October
articles.summary:
Australia's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose to 4.9 per cent in October from 4.7 per cent in September, according to ABS figures reported by the ABC and SBS. Employment fell by about 43,500 and the labour force shrank by 30,400, the ABC reported. Economists had expected the rate to hold steady, SBS said.

The ABC said it is the highest rate since the pandemic. BetaShares economist David Bassanese said the result strengthened the case for the Reserve Bank to hold rates in December. Moody's analysts said most of the fall was in part-time jobs. Opposition Leader Angus Taylor said Australia was in an "economic crisis", according to the ABC.
keyFacts: Unemployment rate rose from 4.7 to 4.9 per cent
Employment fell by about 43,500 in October
Youth unemployment rose to 11.3 per cent

articles.title: Trump and Putin meet on APEC sidelines in Shenzhen; no joint statement issued
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin met on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, according to the ABC and ANI. The ABC reported that Trump greeted Putin with a handshake and said the pair would meet a second time later in the day.

Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the leaders discussed the war in Ukraine and bilateral relations and issued no joint statement, Ukrainian outlet UA.NEWS reported. Ushakov said no major announcements were made because both sides were preparing for the three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The US side had not released its own account in the reports reviewed.
keyFacts: First in-person talks since the 2025 Alaska summit
Kremlin says Ukraine and bilateral ties were discussed
Three-way meeting with Xi was due later on Thursday

articles.title: Anthropic prices IPO at $US83 a share, raising about $US81 billion
articles.summary:
AI company Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $US83 a share, above its expected range of $US70 to $US78, AP reported. The company said on X that the price was set and that trading on Nasdaq was expected to begin on Thursday US time under the ticker ANT.

AP said the sale of 980 million shares, up from 825 million planned, raised about $US81 billion and valued the company at about $US1.5 trillion. AP said that was more than the roughly $US75 billion raised by SpaceX in June. The company's filings describe $US6.2 billion in debt and computing commitments of about $US900 billion, according to AP.
keyFacts: What changed: priced at $US83, above the $US70-$US78 range
Share sale enlarged to 980 million shares
AP reports a valuation of about $US1.5 trillion

articles.title: Trump weighing new strikes on Iran as Israel presses for campaign, NYT reports
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump is considering another round of major strikes on Iran but has not decided, The New York Times reported, citing US and Israeli officials, according to i24NEWS and The Times of Israel. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has urged a four- to seven-day air campaign, the reports said.

Israel's Mossad chief Roman Gofman met US officials in Washington last week with intelligence that Iran is advancing chemical and biological weapons work, according to the reports. Axios reported some US officials believe the intelligence is driven by an agenda. Trump told Fox News there was an indication Iran was looking at gas. Iran has not responded to the reports.
keyFacts: The NYT says Trump has not made a decision
Israel is reported to favour a four- to seven-day campaign
US officials are reported to be divided on the intelligence

articles.title: Crimea bridge hit again overnight as rail traffic halted
articles.summary:
The bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea was hit again just after midnight local time on Thursday, its Moscow-installed head Sergei Aksyonov said, according to the Kyiv Independent. Russia's Transport Ministry said rail traffic was temporarily suspended after a drone attack and no one was hurt, ANI reported, citing TASS.

The strike follows a Ukrainian missile attack on Tuesday that dropped part of the bridge into the Kerch Strait. The Kyiv Independent said it could not independently verify the extent of the latest damage. Aksyonov said general traffic was paused while damage was assessed. Ukraine had not commented on the latest strike in the reports reviewed.
keyFacts: What changed: a further strike overnight on Thursday
Rail traffic suspended, according to Russia
No injuries reported by Russian officials

articles.title: Labor and Coalition block Senate inquiry into electoral funding bill
articles.summary:
Labor and the Coalition voted down independent senator David Pocock's motion to refer the government's electoral reform bill to a Senate committee, the ABC reported. The bill changes political donation and disclosure rules. South Australian Liberal senator Andrew McLachlan crossed the floor to back the referral with the Greens, One Nation and crossbench.

Senate government business manager Katy Gallagher then moved to suspend standing orders to set time limits on debate for five bills, including the electoral bill and a defence bases bill, with votes from 1pm, according to the ABC. Labor's gas reservation, trust tax and capital gains tax bills were not included.
keyFacts: Pocock's referral motion was defeated
One Liberal senator crossed the floor
Five bills listed for a guillotine

articles.title: Xi and Putin hold talks in Shenzhen before meeting Trump
articles.summary:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin held about two hours of talks in Shenzhen before the APEC summit, the BBC reported. Xi said the relationship was stable and the two countries would keep moving forward, according to the BBC.

Xinhua quoted Xi describing a constructive and stable strategic relationship based on respect and equality, the BBC said. Newsweek reported that Xi said the two countries must advance a multipolar world. Putin was greeted at the airport by senior official Cai Qi, while Xi personally greeted US President Donald Trump, according to Newsweek. No agreements from the talks were reported.
keyFacts: Talks lasted about two hours, the BBC said
Held before Trump's arrival in Shenzhen
No agreements announced

articles.title: Marles says government still wants Port of Darwin back as Landbridge refuses to sell
articles.summary:
Acting Prime Minister Richard Marles said the government remains committed to returning the Port of Darwin to Australian hands, but gave no timeline, the ABC and news.com.au reported. Marles said the government wanted operator Landbridge to sell its interest.

Landbridge, a Chinese-owned company that signed a 99-year, $506 million lease in 2015, said it is not a willing seller and that forced divestment would breach international law, news.com.au reported. The ABC said the company has taken international legal action, calling the move discriminatory under the Australia-China free trade agreement. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is due to meet President Xi Jinping on Friday.
keyFacts: Lease signed in 2015 for 99 years
Landbridge says it is not a willing seller
No timeline given for the buyback

articles.title: Government sets up NDIS plan management panel to tighten oversight
articles.summary:
NDIS Minister Jenny McAllister announced a Plan Management Panel to strengthen oversight of providers who manage participants' funds and to target fraud, the ABC reported. The government expects its broader NDIS changes to save $1.4 billion over the forward estimates.

Between July and September, the National Disability Insurance Agency rejected 3,600 claims worth $5.8 million over suspected fraud, misuse or non-compliance, according to the ABC. The ABC report did not include responses from disability advocates or plan managers. Details of how providers will be selected for the panel were not given in the report.
keyFacts: Panel to oversee plan management providers
3,600 claims worth $5.8m rejected July-September
Overhaul expected to save $1.4 billion

articles.title: Bupa closed two GP clinics months after buying them, ABC reports
articles.summary:
Health insurer Bupa closed GP clinics in Belrose in Sydney and Southport on the Gold Coast shortly after buying them, and converted a Seaforth clinic into a mental health centre, the ABC reported. Bupa runs 33 medical clinics and has approval to buy 68 more from Partnered Health.

Bupa said the closures followed a review of local needs, staff were offered redeployment and a hotline was set up to transfer patients, according to the ABC. A former patient and a former receptionist said services declined after the takeover; Bupa rejected claims it neglected the Belrose clinic. RACGP president Michael Wright said practices would become more corporatised.
keyFacts: Belrose clinic closed 15 months after purchase
Bupa has approval to buy 68 Partnered Health clinics
Bupa says patients were helped to transfer

articles.title: Jess Wilson pledges gas exploration process within 60 days if elected
articles.summary:
Victorian Opposition Leader Jess Wilson said she would seek expressions of interest for gas exploration within 60 days if she became premier, the ABC reported. Wilson ruled out changing Victoria's fracking laws.

The Coalition has also promised to lift the payroll tax threshold to $1.2 million, according to the ABC. Neither major party has pledged to return land tax to 2023 levels. Victorian Electoral Commission figures show 211,461 people voted at early voting centres on Wednesday. Labor's response to the gas pledge was not included in the ABC report. Early voting for the state election began this week.
keyFacts: Expressions of interest within 60 days
Fracking laws would not change
211,461 early votes cast on Wednesday

articles.title: Family First disendorses Bendigo West candidate over online posts
articles.summary:
Family First has disendorsed its Bendigo West candidate for the Victorian election, Christos Harisopoulos, over online content the party described as unacceptable, the ABC reported. A post attributed to him made claims about land sales to China by the major parties.

Party national director Lyle Shelton said Family First is a small party with limited resources, according to the ABC. The party disendorsed him on Wednesday afternoon. The ABC said he was the latest candidate in the campaign dropped over social media posts. Harisopoulos' response was not included in the report.
keyFacts: Candidate disendorsed on Wednesday
Party cited unacceptable online content
Shelton cited limited party resources

articles.title: Medics report three killed as Israeli raid continues in central Gaza
articles.summary:
Palestinian medics said an Israeli airstrike near an Israeli ground raid in central Gaza killed one person, and two others were killed by Israeli fire in Deir al-Balah and Gaza City on Thursday, SBS reported, citing Reuters. The Israeli military said it struck a militant in Gaza City and knew of no incident in Deir al-Balah.

The military said troops were dismantling a tunnel west of the ceasefire line. Hamas said the raid and displacement violated the ceasefire. The US-backed body overseeing the truce accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet commitments, according to the report. Gaza health authorities say at least 1,600 people have been killed since the ceasefire.
keyFacts: What changed: medics report three deaths on Thursday
Israel says it is dismantling a tunnel
Hamas says the raid violates the ceasefire

articles.title: Iran says it struck US early-warning radar in Bahrain
articles.summary:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it targeted a US early-warning radar site in Bahrain, describing the strike as retaliation for an air attack on a telecommunications tower in Hormozgan province, Al Jazeera reported. Iranian state media said the port city of Sirik was hit on Thursday. The IRGC-affiliated Fars agency said the radar was destroyed.

The United States and Bahrain had not commented. Reuters said it was the first attack on US military assets in a Gulf country claimed by Iran since early September. US Central Command said its naval blockade of Iranian ports remained in force.
keyFacts: The IRGC called the strike a warning
Neither Washington nor Manama commented
The US blockade of Iranian ports continues

articles.title: Microsoft services recovering; company says no sign outage was a cyber attack
articles.summary:
Microsoft said there was no indication that Friday's global outage of Outlook, Teams and other services was caused by a cyber attack, and reported a gradual recovery from about 10am AEDT, the ABC reported. Microsoft said a process that sets up secure connections on affected servers became overloaded and that it was reviewing recent configuration changes.

The AFP, ASIO, NSW Parliament, Service NSW and Queensland Health were among those affected, according to AAP. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said an agreement with Microsoft to prioritise Australian recovery had been activated. The ABC reported a senior Home Affairs official had warned in August about the impact of a Microsoft outage.
keyFacts: The outage began just after 3am AEDT
National Cyber Security Coordinator is examining it
Government agencies including AFP and ASIO were affected

articles.title: Finland detects strike on Russian warship in Gulf of Finland; Ukraine claims attack
articles.summary:
Finland's military said it detected a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland area and that Finland faced no immediate military threat, Al Jazeera reported, citing Reuters. Finland gave no details on the location or source. Finnish broadcaster Yle reported that Ukraine's Security Service said it carried out the attack.

Local media said the vessel was a small navy ship that returned to St Petersburg; casualties were unclear. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Ireland after talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Kushner said the US was working towards the war's largest prisoner exchange.
keyFacts: Finland said it faced no immediate threat
Ukraine's SBU claimed the attack, according to Yle
Russia said it intercepted 146 drones over Leningrad region

articles.title: Trump says he would consider military force against Cuba before leaving office
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump said in a radio interview with host Hugh Hewitt that he would consider using military force against Cuba and wanted to resolve the issue before his term ends in 2029, Al Jazeera reported. Politico reported it was the first time Trump had given a timeframe for a possible operation. Trump said Secretary of State Marco Rubio would support it.

A US oil blockade of Cuba has been in place since January. Cuban officials have called it collective punishment, and the island has faced nationwide blackouts and shortages. In March, the head of US Southern Command told senators US troops were not rehearsing an invasion.
keyFacts: Trump's term ends in January 2029
A US oil blockade has applied since January
The US has sanctioned President Díaz-Canel

articles.title: Government reconsidering planned backpacker visa changes, Burke indicates
articles.summary:
Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke indicated the government is reworking its planned changes to working holiday visas, the ABC reported. Burke said Australia still needed to reduce numbers and that the overall migration figure he announced could not change, but described the adjustments as tweaks and said a resolution was close.

Home Affairs data show British working holiday arrivals rose from 47,238 in 2023-24 to 79,412 in 2024-25, after a free trade deal removed specified work requirements for UK citizens. The ACCI said businesses needed certainty. Albanese raised the scheme with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham at COP31, according to AAP.
keyFacts: Applications from 24 countries were paused in August
Labor targets net migration of 225,000 by 2028
UK citizens can stay up to three years

articles.title: UN Indigenous rights envoy says youth detention is creating a new Stolen Generation
articles.summary:
The UN Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, Albert Barume, said at the end of his visit to Australia that the detention of Aboriginal children amounted to a new Stolen Generation, AAP reported. He said he was refused access to Darwin's Holtze and Queensland's Cleveland youth detention centres, and called on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to show leadership.

A Senate report found that in the June 2025 quarter, 60 per cent of children in detention were Indigenous, compared with 6.6 per cent of the population. Barume is due to report to the UN Human Rights Council in September 2027.
keyFacts: Barume's visit ended on Friday
He said he was denied access to two centres
His report is due in September 2027

articles.title: ASX falls nearly 1 per cent at midday; Australian dollar at lowest since January
articles.summary:
The S&P/ASX 200 was down 83.4 points, or 0.91 per cent, at 9,063.4 at midday on Friday, AAP reported, with financials down more than 1 per cent. A Capital.com analyst said Nvidia's leadership upheaval had slowed a recovery in technology shares.

Brent crude rose to about US$96 a barrel after President Trump's comments on Iran talks, while gold fell to a 13-month low near US$3,883 an ounce and copper reached its lowest level since July. The Australian dollar traded at 68.02 US cents, its lowest since January, according to AAP.
keyFacts: ASX 200 at midday: 9,063.4
Gold at a 13-month low
Australian dollar: 68.02 US cents

articles.title: Death toll from Brooklyn building collapse rises to at least eight
articles.summary:
At least eight people, including two children, died when a three-storey building collapsed into a neighbouring construction site in the Flatbush area of Brooklyn, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said, according to Al Jazeera. At least 18 people were taken to hospital, four in a critical condition, and about 250 firefighters attended.

The Fire Department said the cause was under investigation. City records cited in the report show a stop-work order was issued for the adjacent site in March, work resumed in violation in April, and it was allowed to continue in May. The architect, owner and contractor did not respond to AP.
keyFacts: The collapse happened on Wednesday afternoon local time
At least 18 people were hospitalised
A stop-work order was issued in March

articles.title: Spanish court suspends far-right group Núcleo Nacional in hate crime probe
articles.summary:
A judge in the northern Spanish city of Gijón suspended the activities of the far-right group Núcleo Nacional on Thursday, ordering its office closed and its social media and bank accounts blocked as part of an investigation into alleged hate crimes and illegal association, Al Jazeera reported, citing Reuters.

Fourteen members were arrested last week on suspicion of inciting hatred, and police said they seized more than 20 firearms from the group's Madrid headquarters. A representative of the group said in a video that it faced political persecution. Spain holds a general election on 29 November.
keyFacts: 14 members were arrested last week
Police seized more than 20 firearms
Spain votes on 29 November

articles.title: NSW inquiry hears from Bondi attack survivor and gun sellers on firearm law repeal bill
articles.summary:
Bondi terror attack survivor Leon Elski told a NSW parliamentary inquiry into a bill to repeal the state's new gun restrictions that he supported the reforms and stronger licence checks, AAP reported. He said the existing system had failed despite several layers of checks.

Gun retailers told the inquiry the changes, including a cap on firearms per person and a buyback, were damaging their businesses. The Shooters Union and the Australian Jewish Association backed repeal. Premier Chris Minns introduced the restrictions after the 14 December 2025 attack, in which 15 people were killed.
keyFacts: The inquiry is examining a repeal bill
Reforms include a per-person firearms cap
The Bondi attack killed 15 people

articles.title: SA energy minister supports gas helping power proposed AI data centres
articles.summary:
South Australian Energy Minister Tom Koutsantonis told the ABC he was comfortable with gas being used to firm power supply for proposed AI data centres when solar and wind output is low. The state's data centre strategy, released about five months ago, focused on renewable energy.

SA Greens leader Rob Simms called the position a reversal and proposed a moratorium, which a government spokesperson rejected. The Conservation Council called gas a step backwards, while Data Centres Australia defended its use. Developer Quantum DC paused its 1,200-megawatt Tungkillo proposal on 12 November.
keyFacts: Quantum DC estimated 20 per cent gas use
Iren has proposed an 800MW site at Bundey
The Greens want a data centre moratorium

articles.title: NSW Supreme Court allows Rising Tide flotilla on Newcastle Harbour
articles.summary:
NSW Supreme Court Justice Edward Muston dismissed a police application to prohibit Rising Tide's anti-coal flotilla on Newcastle Harbour, finding the public interest in political expression outweighed the commissioner's safety concerns, the ABC reported. The protest is capped at 785 watercraft and will block the shipping channel for 30 to 40 minutes.

Police argued the risk of collision, capsize and drowning was serious. Rising Tide's barrister pointed to safety teams and mandatory life jackets, and an organiser said there would be no civil disobedience.
keyFacts: The ruling was made on Friday
Up to 785 watercraft may take part
The channel will be blocked for up to 40 minutes

articles.title: Tasmanian Premier apologises for effect of post about school Christmas events
articles.summary:
Tasmanian Premier Jeremy Rockliff apologised for the effect of an October Facebook post that said Christmas references were being removed from school celebrations, the ABC reported. The school concerned was identified online, called security over abuse, and its acting principal took leave.

The Australian Education Union had passed a no-confidence motion in Rockliff and barred politicians from school events until he apologised. The Education Department secretary had written to Rockliff on the day of the post saying Christmas remained important. Rockliff said he stood by his expectations and did not retract the claim.
keyFacts: The post was made on 14 October
The AEU passed a no-confidence motion
Rockliff did not withdraw the claim

articles.title: AAP FactCheck finds overseas-run pages invented Albanese–Allan feud
articles.summary:
AAP FactCheck found false a claim that former Victorian premier Jacinta Allan publicly called for Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to be removed. The posts came from a Facebook page that Meta's transparency data shows is run from Vietnam.

AAP said there was no record of such a statement. It also found no Hansard record of a claimed exchange between Bob Katter and Fatima Payman, and said a reported on-air clash between Albanese and Michael Rowland did not occur; Rowland left the ABC in February. Similar claims appeared on other pages ahead of the 28 November Victorian election.
keyFacts: The page is run from Vietnam, Meta data show
Allan lost the Labor leadership in July
Images showed signs of AI generation

articles.title: US Supreme Court agrees to rule on Trump's asylum ban at the Mexican border
articles.summary:
The US Supreme Court agreed on Friday to decide whether President Donald Trump acted lawfully when he suspended asylum access for migrants crossing the southern border between ports of entry, according to Reuters and CBS News. The restrictions were set out in a proclamation on his first day in office.

A federal judge in Washington ruled against the policy in July 2025, and an appeals court upheld that ruling in April, but the restrictions have largely stayed in force while the case continues, Reuters reported. Immigrant rights groups brought the challenge. A ruling is expected by the end of June.
keyFacts: Policy dates from Trump's 20 January 2025 proclamation
Two lower courts ruled against the restrictions
Decision expected by the end of June

articles.title: Ukraine fires nearly 1,200 drones at Russia; Kushner says Europe will join talks
articles.summary:
Ukraine launched almost 1,200 drones at Russian targets overnight into Friday, one of its largest aerial attacks of the war, AP reported. Russia's Defence Ministry said 1,198 were shot down. Local officials said strikes on three Russian regions killed seven people, including a 12-year-old. Ukrainian authorities said Russia fired 117 drones at Ukraine, killing at least two.

After talks in Abu Dhabi, US envoy Jared Kushner said Russia had agreed that Europe would be included in coming negotiations. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Europe should insist on a ceasefire first. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow was open to contacts once it understood European intentions.
keyFacts: Russia says it downed 1,198 Ukrainian drones
Seven killed in three Russian regions, officials said
Russia launched 117 drones at Ukraine overnight

articles.title: US producer prices rise 6.5 per cent over the year, the fastest pace since 2022
articles.summary:
US producer prices rose 0.3 per cent in October, below the 0.4 per cent economists had forecast, according to Labor Department figures reported by Investing.com and Yahoo Finance. Over the year to October, prices were up 6.5 per cent, the largest annual increase since November 2022.

Goods prices rose 0.5 per cent in the month and services 0.2 per cent, Investing.com reported. Analysts at Capital Economics said the Federal Reserve may need to raise rates more quickly. Markets are pricing in at least a quarter-point rise at the Fed's December meeting, with some bets on half a point.
keyFacts: Monthly rise of 0.3 per cent, below forecasts
Annual rise of 6.5 per cent, up from 6.3 per cent
Markets expect a Fed rate rise in December

articles.title: Wall Street slips as chip stocks fall and US 10-year yield tops 5.1 per cent
articles.summary:
US shares fell on Friday as chipmakers sold off after Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia chief executive, AP reported. In afternoon trading the S&P 500 was down 0.6 per cent, the Nasdaq 1.1 per cent and the Dow 0.1 per cent. AP said the S&P 500 was still on track for a weekly gain of about 2 per cent.

Nvidia was down 2.8 per cent, Broadcom 5.1 per cent and AMD 10 per cent at that point, according to AP. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.14 per cent from 5.10 per cent. Economists widely expect the Federal Reserve to raise rates in December, AP reported.
keyFacts: AMD down about 10 per cent in afternoon trade
10-year Treasury yield at 5.14 per cent
Figures are afternoon levels, not final closes

articles.title: US military denies Iran hit radar in Bahrain, says it shot down two drones
articles.summary:
The US military denied an Iranian claim that the Revolutionary Guards had destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, Reuters reported. US forces said they shot down two one-way attack drones launched towards Bahrain by the Guards and that no harm was caused.

Iran said its action was retaliation for an air strike on a telecommunications tower near the port town of Sirik in Hormozgan province, according to Iranian state media cited by Reuters and RFE/RL. There was no immediate comment from Bahrain. The war began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran on 28 February, and the US has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports.
keyFacts: US says two Iranian drones were shot down
Iran cited a strike on a tower near Sirik
Bahrain did not immediately comment

articles.title: Iran says LNG tanker hit a mine and exploded in the Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said a tanker carrying liquefied natural gas struck a naval mine and exploded in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, according to Iranian state media cited by Reuters. The Guards said the ship had taken an unauthorised and dangerous route. No details about the vessel were immediately available.

The report came a day after Iranian media said four oil tankers had been hit by explosions. Reuters, citing the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, said at least 10 ships were hit in the first 10 days of November, after 37 attacks in October.
keyFacts: Iran says the ship used an unauthorised route
Four tankers were reported hit the previous day
At least 10 ships hit in early November, think tank says

articles.title: US Senate committee asks Jensen Huang and Howard Lutnick to testify over Nvidia case
articles.summary:
Senate Banking Committee chair Tim Scott has asked former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang to appear on 3 December and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on 10 December, Fortune reported. Scott's letter cited national security concerns and said the committee was prepared to use subpoenas if they did not appear voluntarily.

Huang resigned this week after acknowledging an affair with a woman reported to be suspected by US intelligence of spying for China, which has denied involvement. Reuters, citing unnamed sources, reported a second relationship with an employee. Senators from both parties have raised questions about the Commerce Department's handling of chip exports to China, Fortune said.
keyFacts: Huang asked to appear on 3 December
Lutnick asked to appear on 10 December
Committee says it may use subpoenas

articles.title: Poland says Pentagon backs permanent US troop base; White House to decide in December
articles.summary:
Poland's Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said the Pentagon had given a green light to a permanent US troop presence in Poland, with a final White House decision expected in early December, according to Military Times and Breaking Defense. He spoke after meeting US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on 10 November.

The Pentagon's readout of the meeting did not mention a base. Warsaw has proposed four possible sites, Bydgoszcz, Poznań, Szczecin and Wrocław, for about 5,000 US troops, and has offered to fund infrastructure estimated at up to US$4.4 billion, Breaking Defense reported. Poland hosts about 10,000 mostly rotational US soldiers.
keyFacts: Final decision expected from White House in early December
Base proposed for about 5,000 US troops
Pentagon readout did not mention a base

articles.title: Dutch coalition survives crisis talks after row over tax package
articles.summary:
Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten held about seven hours of crisis talks on Friday with leaders of his two coalition partners after a dispute over a tax package, AP and NL Times reported. Sources told NL Times the conservative VVD would stay in the minority government.

The row began when coalition partners D66 and CDA passed an amended tax plan with support from left-leaning opposition parties, while the VVD voted against it. VVD leader Dilan Yeşilgöz-Zegerius said the minority cabinet experiment had failed but adjustments were possible, AP reported. Jetten said further talks would be held in the coming days. The government took office less than nine months ago.
keyFacts: Talks lasted about seven hours, NL Times said
Tax plan passed with a one-vote majority
Government is less than nine months old

articles.title: US moves to seize $1.2b in crypto stolen from Binance, blames North Korea
articles.summary:
The US Justice Department said it had obtained court authorisation to seize or restrain more than US$1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from the Binance exchange in late October. The FBI attributes the theft, of more than US$6 billion, to a North Korea-linked group it calls TraderTraitor.

Government and private-sector efforts have frozen more than US$2.7 billion in total, the department said. It also said it had seized cloud infrastructure used in a separate scheme, called FaceStealer, which it says stole more than US$400 million over 18 months. CBS News reported that a judge would later decide who has a legitimate claim to recovered funds.
keyFacts: More than US$6 billion was taken from Binance
US$2.7 billion frozen in total, officials said
Separate FaceStealer scheme blamed for US$400m theft

articles.title: Albanese leaves COP31 for ASEAN summit, where Trump is due to attend
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese left the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday night Australian time for the ASEAN summit in the Philippines, AAP reported. US President Donald Trump is confirmed to attend the ASEAN event on 17 November, and the two leaders could meet up to three times across ASEAN and the APEC forum in Shenzhen, according to AAP.

Albanese is expected to discuss regional security and fuel supplies, AAP said. Environmental groups criticised the government at COP31 for not addressing a fossil fuel phase-out. Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen remains in Turkey as head of negotiations, with a cover decision due on 20 November.
keyFacts: Trump confirmed for ASEAN event on 17 November
Trip ends at APEC in Shenzhen, China
Bowen stays at COP31 to lead negotiations

articles.title: Microsoft apologises for near 24-hour outage, blames network capacity upgrade
articles.summary:
Microsoft has apologised for an outage that disrupted Outlook, Teams, OneDrive and other Microsoft 365 services for close to 24 hours, according to Windows Central and AAP. The company said the problem was technical and not related to a cyber attack or AI. It linked the fault to an earlier network capacity upgrade and said it would publish a full incident report.

In Australia, ASIO chief Mike Burgess said ASIO and the AFP were affected, mainly through email, AAP reported. NSW Parliament, Service NSW, Queensland Health and Northern Territory government services were also hit. In the UK, the NHS and London's Metropolitan Police were affected.
keyFacts: Restoration took almost 24 hours
Microsoft says there was no cyber attack
Full post-incident report promised

articles.title: Car bomb in Moscow injures former aide to ex-Ukrainian prime minister
articles.summary:
A car explosion in Moscow's Chertanovo district injured Sergei Zavorotny, a former adviser to former Ukrainian prime minister Mykola Azarov, Russian authorities said on Friday, according to Anadolu Agency and Al Jazeera. Russia's Investigative Committee opened a criminal case. It was the second car bombing in Russia in two days, after a blast in St Petersburg killed a serviceman, Al Jazeera reported.

Azarov said he believed Ukrainian services were behind the attack. Moscow blames Kyiv for such attacks; Ukrainian authorities had not commented. No group has claimed responsibility. Russian broadcaster REN TV reported serious injuries, which officials did not confirm.
keyFacts: Investigative Committee opened a criminal case
Second car bombing in Russia in two days
No group has claimed responsibility

articles.title: UK jury convicts man wanted by Germany over alleged Hamas-linked plot of wounding bailiff
articles.summary:
A jury at Birmingham Crown Court convicted Mohammed Al Fatih, 40, of wounding a debt collector on Friday and acquitted him of wounding with intent, The National reported. He was remanded for sentencing, and extradition proceedings will resume.

German federal prosecutors allege he was one of eight men plotting attacks on Jewish targets and Israeli diplomats, and that he stored pistols in Vienna, according to The National. Those allegations have not been tested in court. Israel's Mossad says his father is senior Hamas figure Basem Naim. His barrister argued post-traumatic stress explained his behaviour during the incident. He was granted UK asylum in 2015.
keyFacts: Acquitted of the more serious charge of intent
Germany is seeking his extradition
German allegations remain untested in court

articles.title: Spain sets Sánchez–Feijóo election debate for 19 November
articles.summary:
Spain's Television Academy said Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez of the Socialist party and opposition People's Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo will hold a televised debate on Thursday 19 November, according to the EFE news agency and El Español. The academy's president, María Casado, will moderate.

The parties agreed on five topics: housing, economy and tax, social policy and public services, anti-corruption and democratic renewal, and migration and foreign policy, EFE reported. A draw decided Feijóo will open and Sánchez will close. El Español said the debate was originally planned for 16 November. Spain holds a general election on 29 November.
keyFacts: Debate moved from 16 to 19 November
Five agreed topic blocks, including housing
General election is on 29 November

articles.title: France criticises Israel's entry ban on Jean-Luc Mélenchon
articles.summary:
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot called Israel's decision to bar left-wing leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon from entering the country a demagogic move, Middle East Eye reported. Israel announced the ban on Thursday, citing his statements on Israel and the Gaza war.

Israeli Interior Minister Gideon Sa'ar accused Mélenchon of spreading blood libels, referring among other things to his pledge to escort aid flotillas to Gaza if elected, according to Middle East Eye. Mélenchon said on X that he had been barred from a place he had no plans to visit. Barrot, a political opponent of Mélenchon, said the decision helped Mélenchon's party.
keyFacts: Israel announced the ban on Thursday
Barrot is a political opponent of Mélenchon
Mélenchon is a 2027 presidential contender

articles.title: Pakistan army says 74 militants killed in raids since 3 November
articles.summary:
Pakistan's military media wing said security forces had killed at least 74 militants since 3 November in operations in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan provinces, Arab News Pakistan reported. It said 35 were killed in Mir Ali and eight in Orakzai in the previous 48 hours, and that weapons and explosives were recovered.

The military described militants in Balochistan as backed by India, which New Delhi denies. Pakistan also accuses Afghanistan of sheltering Pakistani Taliban fighters, which Kabul denies. The military said operations would continue. The figures could not be independently verified.
keyFacts: 43 killed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 48 hours
India and Afghanistan deny Pakistan's accusations
Military says operations will continue

articles.title: Ten killed in Guinea clashes over ban on artisanal gold mining
articles.summary:
Ten people were killed and 13 injured in clashes in Guinea's Siguiri gold region as security forces enforced a ban on unregulated artisanal mining, according to provisional government figures reported by Mining.com. Five of the dead were foreign nationals. The territorial administration ministry said protesters had set up barricades before gunfire broke out.

More than 1,200 suspected illegal miners have been arrested since the ban took effect on 2 November, Mining.com reported. Malian authorities said about 160,000 people had been displaced into Mali, and Burkina Faso said it had repatriated more than 45,000 citizens from Guinea.
keyFacts: Ban on artisanal mining took effect 2 November
Five foreign nationals among the dead
More than 1,200 suspected miners arrested

articles.title: Democrat Cindy Holscher wins Kansas governor's race, AP declares
articles.summary:
Democrat Cindy Holscher has won the Kansas governorship, defeating Republican state Senate president Ty Masterson, according to an AP race call reported by PBS NewsHour. She succeeds term-limited Democratic Governor Laura Kelly.

Holscher campaigned on halting construction of new AI data centres, AP reported. Republicans outspent Democrats by more than three to one, with the Republican Governors Association spending US$19 million on advertising, according to AdImpact data cited by AP. In other Kansas races, Democrats won a US Senate seat for the first time since 1932 and Chris Mann defeated Attorney General Kris Kobach.
keyFacts: Holscher succeeds Democrat Laura Kelly
Republicans outspent Democrats three to one
Democrats also won a US Senate seat in Kansas

articles.title: Mamdani says Trump agreed to delay new SNAP stocking rules for small shops
articles.summary:
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said on Friday he had reached a deal directly with President Donald Trump to delay enforcement of new federal food stamp (SNAP) stocking rules for small retailers nationwide, amNY reported. City Hall said the delay is 90 days.

The rules require participating stores to stock more varieties of staple foods. Mamdani had written to the Agriculture Department on 2 November asking for a six-month delay. The White House and the department had not confirmed the agreement when amNY published. The city says more than 10,000 New York bodegas and corner stores are affected.
keyFacts: Delay is 90 days, City Hall says
White House had not confirmed the deal
Rules affect small SNAP retailers nationwide

articles.title: White House says Trump, Xi and Putin will meet together at APEC in China
articles.summary:
The White House has confirmed plans for a three-way meeting between US President Donald Trump, China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of next week's APEC summit in Shenzhen, according to AAP and Al Jazeera. It would be the first such meeting of the three leaders.

Trump has said the talks could cover the US war with Iran and a new nuclear arms agreement that includes China, after the New START treaty with Russia expired in February. A senior US official told Reuters no agreement is expected. The Kremlin called the meeting significant. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has raised concern about decisions being made without Kyiv.
keyFacts: Meeting planned on APEC sidelines in Shenzhen
New START expired in February
US official says no agreement expected

articles.title: FAA halts all US departures for over four hours after air traffic communications fault
articles.summary:
The US Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop on Friday, US time, after a communications problem affected air traffic control centres, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said. The stop lasted more than four hours before departures resumed, according to AAP and the ABC.

The ABC reported more than 11,000 flights were delayed or cancelled and about 600 diverted. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said early findings pointed to a telecommunications failure, with no sign of an attack so far. Duffy said US$30 billion is needed to upgrade air traffic control. Australian travel industry representatives said travellers due to fly within 72 hours were being prioritised.
keyFacts: Ground stop lasted more than four hours
ABC reports 11,000+ flights delayed or cancelled
Officials say no sign of an attack so far

articles.title: Australia and Philippines to sign defence cooperation agreement in Manila
articles.summary:
Australia and the Philippines are expected to sign a defence cooperation agreement on Sunday on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit in Manila, the ABC and SBS reported. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese arrived in Manila on Saturday from the COP31 climate summit in Türkiye.

According to the ABC, the deal is expected to expand reciprocal military access and information sharing and support the Philippine navy and coastguard. SBS reported it would cover maritime awareness and interoperability. China's foreign ministry has told Australia to stop inciting confrontation, the ABC said. Albanese may meet US President Donald Trump, who is due at ASEAN on 17 November, AAP reported.
keyFacts: Signing expected Sunday in Manila
Covers military access and information sharing
Trump due at ASEAN on 17 November

articles.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said two oil tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, according to a statement on Iranian state television reported by ANI and Aaj News. It said one was a supertanker and that both had switched off radar and positioning systems to cross by an unauthorised route.

Iran did not name the ships or their flags, and the claims have not been independently confirmed. The US military has said it has cleared the main shipping lanes of mines. Al Jazeera described it as the third reported tanker incident in about 24 hours.
keyFacts: Ships and flags were not named
Claims not independently confirmed
US says main lanes cleared of mines

articles.title: ICC judges close part of Afghanistan probe that covered alleged US troop crimes
articles.summary:
Judges at the International Criminal Court have closed the part of the prosecutor's Afghanistan investigation that could examine alleged crimes by US forces, along with a probe into the Islamic State affiliate ISIS-K, according to Reuters and AP reports carried by Al Jazeera and Defense News. The investigation will now focus on the Taliban's conduct since 2021.

The judges cited significant limits on the prosecution's ability to investigate. The prosecutor's office said it had appealed. The US is not an ICC member and has sanctioned court staff. Arrest warrants for four Taliban leaders remain in force, Reuters reported.
keyFacts: Focus narrowed to Taliban conduct since 2021
Prosecutor's office has appealed
Warrants for four Taliban leaders remain

articles.title: Türkiye and Qatar sign mutual defence agreement
articles.summary:
Türkiye and Qatar have signed a mutual defence agreement committing them to a unified position against any external armed attack on either country, according to AFP and Al Jazeera. It was signed after President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan met Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani in Istanbul on Friday.

A joint statement carried by Qatar's state news agency said the pact covers consultation on threats, joint exercises, defence industry cooperation and training, AFP reported. Erdoğan's office said it added a new dimension to ties, and the emir called it a strategic partnership. Other agreements signed included one on conflict resolution.
keyFacts: Signed in Istanbul on Friday
Pledges joint stance against external attack
Covers exercises, industry and training

articles.title: US gives states six more months before enforcing Medicaid work requirements
articles.summary:
The Trump administration said on Friday, US time, that states will have six more months before they must enforce new Medicaid work requirements, moving enforcement to 1 July 2027, STAT reported. States had been preparing to start on 1 January.

The rules, from last year's budget law, require many working-age adults covered under Medicaid expansion to work, study or volunteer 80 hours a month unless exempt. STAT reported that states had sued the federal health agency CMS seeking a delay until exemptions for medically frail people were settled, and that a judge recently rejected the administration's definition of medical frailty.
keyFacts: Enforcement moved to 1 July 2027
Requirement is 80 hours a month
States had sued seeking a delay

articles.title: New York Fed report confirms US Treasury bought yen in July
articles.summary:
The US Treasury bought Japanese yen in the July–September quarter while the Federal Reserve made no foreign exchange interventions of its own, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York said in its quarterly report. Reuters reported the New York Fed bought 79.4 billion yen for the Treasury on 31 July, paid for with euros from the Exchange Stabilization Fund.

Japan's Finance Ministry spent 15.4 trillion yen on intervention in the same quarter, according to Reuters. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in August the US would not hesitate to join further action. The yen has since weakened back towards 160 per US dollar, Reuters said.
keyFacts: 79.4 billion yen bought on 31 July
Fed made no interventions of its own
Japan spent 15.4 trillion yen in the quarter

sources.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York (via InsuranceNewsNet)

articles.title: Houthis say they fired missiles at Saudi forces in Jazan
articles.summary:
Yemen's Houthis said on Friday they fired two ballistic missiles at Saudi forces at Al-Tuwal in Jazan province, Reuters reported. The claim came hours after Saudi civil defence declared an all-clear in the province, and Reuters said it was unclear if the two were linked. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation.

The Houthis also claimed attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and on a pumping station on the East-West oil pipeline, according to Reuters. Saudi Arabia has been rerouting about 4 million barrels of oil a day through that pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu.
keyFacts: Houthis claim two ballistic missiles fired
No immediate Saudi confirmation
Airport and pipeline attacks also claimed

articles.title: India targets 900 gigawatts of clean power by 2035 as coal use continues
articles.summary:
India has set a goal of 900 gigawatts of non-fossil power capacity by 2035, almost double its 500-gigawatt target for 2030, AP reported. Its current clean capacity is just over 300 gigawatts, third behind China and the US.

A University of California, Berkeley researcher told AP the target cannot be met unless the grid is upgraded. The government has approved nearly US$20 billion for grid and storage projects. Coal produced about 71 per cent of India's electricity in 2025, according to the think tank Ember, and the head of India's Central Electricity Authority said up to 150 gigawatts of new coal may be needed by 2035.
keyFacts: Target nearly doubles 2030 goal
Current clean capacity just over 300GW
Coal supplied about 71% of 2025 power

articles.title: Victorian Labor pledges $1.17 billion for school upgrades if re-elected
articles.summary:
Victorian Labor would spend more than $1.17 billion upgrading 228 public schools if re-elected, Premier Ben Carroll said on Saturday, AAP reported. The package includes $500 million for non-government schools, made up of $350 million for Catholic schools and $150 million for low-fee independent schools.

Education Minister Gabrielle Williams asked Opposition Leader Jess Wilson which upgrades she would cut. Wilson has alleged the government made secret cuts to non-government school funding, which Labor denies, saying it was keeping funding within national entitlements. Wilson described the pledge as another large pre-election promise, according to AAP.
keyFacts: 228 public schools to be upgraded
$500m for non-government schools
Opposition alleges funding cuts; Labor denies

articles.title: ProPublica reports Georgia election board members worked with Cleta Mitchell network
articles.summary:
Current and former members of Georgia's State Election Board coordinated with lawyer Cleta Mitchell's Election Integrity Network and allied groups, ProPublica reported, citing recordings of private calls and events. It reported that the board's executive director, James Mills, worked closely with network members, according to five sources.

Board chair John Fervier told ProPublica the network's influence should stop. Vice chair Janelle King said activists did not influence her decisions, and Mills declined to answer questions. Mitchell praised the network's work with the board, and network figure Garland Favorito called the report's central claim a false conspiracy theory.
keyFacts: Based on recordings of private calls
Board chair says influence should stop
Network figure calls claim false

articles.title: Zelenskiy says US raised idea of Ukraine leaving Donbas in exchange for NATO entry
articles.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said US negotiators asked whether Kyiv would pull its forces out of the Donbas region if Ukraine were admitted to NATO, according to Reuters and AAP. He said it was the first time membership had been tied to territorial concessions in the talks.

Zelenskiy said Ukraine was not ready to give up territory, but would put such a question to a referendum if it received a full package of security guarantees, military support and reconstruction funding. He also said Russian President Vladimir Putin did not personally support a ceasefire. Moscow's response to the idea was not reported.
keyFacts: Two days of US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi ended without a major breakthrough
The sides agreed a prisoner exchange of more than 1,000 people, Reuters reported
EU leaders named Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland and EU officials as Europe's negotiating team

articles.title: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years
articles.summary:
The United States no longer qualifies as having eliminated measles, according to a decision by an expert commission reporting to the Pan American Health Organization, CBS News and CNN reported on Friday US time. The Wall Street Journal first reported the finding. The US had held the status since 2000.

CBS said the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has counted 5,412 cases in 2026, the most since 1991, and at least six deaths, while state health departments have reported 10 deaths, according to Al Jazeera. The CDC says 96 per cent of this year's infections were in people who were unvaccinated or whose status was unknown. PAHO is due to hold a news conference on Tuesday.
keyFacts: Status is lost when one chain of transmission continues for more than 12 months
Cases have been confirmed in 45 states and Washington DC, CBS said
Kindergarten vaccination fell from 95.2 to 92.4 per cent between 2019-20 and 2025-26, Al Jazeera reported

articles.title: US flight disruption continues; Duffy says contractor router flooded FAA network
articles.summary:
US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a router installed during work by contractor L3Harris at a remote Federal Aviation Administration site began flooding other routers in the air traffic control network, causing Friday's nationwide ground stop, according to Yahoo News. He said officials were still determining whether the cause was contractor error or faulty equipment, and that it was not a cyber attack.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said 4,000 to 5,000 of about 41,000 scheduled flights would be cancelled on Saturday, with schedules expected to return to normal by the end of Sunday. New York Governor Kathy Hochul called for Duffy to resign. L3Harris's response was not reported.
keyFacts: Flightradar24 counted nearly 10,000 cancellations from the stoppage, ABC reported
Bedford said the ground stop was the longest since 11 September 2001
Airlines will not have to compensate passengers because the fault was in FAA systems, ABC said

articles.title: UN says at least 25 seafarers killed around Strait of Hormuz since February
articles.summary:
At least 25 seafarers have been killed in and around the Strait of Hormuz since the US-Israeli war with Iran began in February, UN Assistant Secretary-General Khaled Khiari told the Security Council on Friday, according to Al Jazeera. He said the situation should not be allowed to become normal.

The International Maritime Organization recorded 136 security incidents involving ships between 1 March and 11 November, including 35 in October and 10 so far in November, Khiari said. Iranian authorities said on Saturday that three oil tankers had hit mines in restricted areas, while the US military says the main shipping routes have been cleared.
keyFacts: Figures cover the period up to 11 November
Shipping through the strait is about 65 per cent below pre-war levels, according to UKMTO
Iran and the US give conflicting accounts of whether the routes are safe

articles.title: Hungary recovers nearly $US20 million in cash in probe of Orbán-era minister
articles.summary:
Hungarian authorities have recovered almost $US20 million in cash in a bribery investigation into Miklós Seszták, a development minister under former prime minister Viktor Orbán, Reuters reported. Some of the money was buried in forests and some hidden in farm buildings and warehouses, according to the report. Seszták denies wrongdoing.

Prime Minister Péter Magyar, who replaced Orbán after April's election, described the find as the end of a Fidesz "mafia". Fidesz's response was not included in the Reuters report. Two former ministers and former central bank governor György Matolcsy are under arrest in separate cases and deny wrongdoing.
keyFacts: Recovered sums were 5.07 billion forints, €2.66 million and $US1.26 million
Orbán governed for 16 years before losing power in April
A Median survey puts Fidesz support at 16 per cent, Reuters said

articles.title: COP31: UN climate chief urges faster progress as ministers arrive in Antalya
articles.summary:
UN climate chief Simon Stiell described progress at the COP31 talks in Antalya as constructive on Saturday and urged governments to move quickly to the hardest issues, according to Climate Home News and Reuters. A stocktaking plenary chaired by Türkiye and Australia was scheduled for Saturday night as ministers arrived for the final week.

At least 15 countries have backed a voluntary pledge to lift electricity's share of global final energy use to 35 per cent by 2035, from 23 per cent now, Climate Home reported. African nations are seeking adaptation finance of at least $US120 billion a year by 2035. Civil society groups criticised a draft note on a just transition mechanism, which Chris Bowen called comprehensive.
keyFacts: Australia's Chris Bowen is president of negotiations
EU negotiator Wopke Hoekstra signalled the EU may drop the word 'clean' from electrification wording
Brazil's President Lula said Brazil should host the next fossil fuel phase-out conference

articles.title: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins elected Alaska governor
articles.summary:
Former state legislator Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins has been elected governor of Alaska, the first Democrat to win the office since 1998, according to CBS News and the Associated Press. He defeated three Republican candidates, including one endorsed by President Donald Trump, after more than a week of counting.

Kreiss-Tomkins, 37, said the state had been poorly served under outgoing Republican Governor Mike Dunleavy, citing ferry service cuts, and pledged a cabinet drawing on Republicans, Democrats and independents. Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski endorsed him a week before polling day. Responses from his Republican opponents were not included in the CBS report.
keyFacts: Alaska voted on 3 November
Democrats will hold 30 governorships after the midterms, CBS said
Three former Alaska governors backed Kreiss-Tomkins

articles.title: Alaska voters reject repeal of ranked-choice voting and open primaries
articles.summary:
A ballot measure to repeal Alaska's open top-four primaries and ranked-choice general elections has failed, according to an Associated Press call reported by NPR. It is the second time voters have rejected a repeal, after a 2024 measure failed by 743 votes, Alaska Public Media reported.

Supporters of repeal argued the system is confusing, while opponents of repeal said it gives voters more choice, according to Alaska Public Media. The campaign against repeal raised about $10.4 million, compared with about $2.6 million for the repeal side, the outlet reported. Nick Troiano of Unite America said Alaskans had spoken.
keyFacts: The measure was Ballot Measure 2 at the 3 November election
Elon Musk gave $1.5 million to a group backing repeal, Alaska Public Media said
The US Senate race has two candidates named Dan Sullivan and may go to ranked tabulation, NPR said

articles.title: Report card finds Australia making no progress on reducing rabbit numbers
articles.summary:
Australia's rabbit numbers, spread and impacts have remained largely unchanged over five years, according to the government-compiled Vertebrate Pest Management Report Card, AAP reported. Populations have increased in Victoria, Tasmania and the ACT, and environmental damage is worsening in NSW and Tasmania.

Experts estimate there are about 200 million rabbits nationally, threatening 322 listed species and causing more than $200 million a year in farm losses, AAP said. The federal Established Pest Animals and Weeds program had no ongoing funding in the last budget, with a decision due next year. Reece Pianta of the Invasive Species Council said funding cuts were allowing populations to spread. A government response was not reported.
keyFacts: Rabbits are becoming resistant to the haemorrhagic disease virus released almost a decade ago
The government funded $2.6 million for new biocontrol research this year
Rabbits were released in Victoria in 1859

articles.title: Health leaders back 2040 goal to end rheumatic heart disease as Australia faces criticism
articles.summary:
Global health leaders have backed a Perth Declaration aiming to eliminate rheumatic heart disease and acute rheumatic fever by 2040, the ABC reported. Experts said Australia appears willing to tolerate some of the world's highest rates of the disease, mainly among First Nations people.

About 12,000 people in Australia live with the disease or have a history of rheumatic fever, and First Nations people make up four in five cases, according to the ABC. World Heart Federation president Jagat Narula said Australia had committed only a small part of the $689 million needed for its national strategy. The federal government said it is investing $95.8 million, and Assistant Minister Rebecca White pointed to housing and sanitation work.
keyFacts: First Nations people die from the disease at more than five times the non-Indigenous rate
Australia's national Endgame Strategy targets 2031
Acute rheumatic fever can be treated with penicillin, a Heart Foundation adviser said

articles.title: Australia and the Philippines sign updated defence cooperation agreement
articles.summary:
Australia and the Philippines have signed a defence cooperation agreement in Manila during Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's visit, according to the Manila Times and Rappler. The deal updates a defence arrangement between the two countries that dates from 1995.

Rappler and other outlets reported the updated agreement is meant to speed up coordination between the two militaries, including for disaster response. Bloomberg, via the Japan Times, reported the upgrade comes as both countries focus on China's activity in the region. Mr Albanese travels on to the ASEAN summit, where US President Donald Trump is due to attend, AAP reported. Beijing's response was not reported in the sources reviewed.
keyFacts: The agreement updates a 1995 defence arrangement
It was signed in Manila on 15 November
The signing was flagged by both governments on 14 November

articles.title: Iran's navy says three oil tankers hit mines in Hormuz and are on fire
articles.summary:
Iran's navy has said three oil tankers struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire, according to Arab News, Middle East Eye and the Manila Times. A day earlier, Iran's Revolutionary Guards had said two oil tankers hit mines in the strait.

The vessels' names, flags and any casualties were not independently confirmed in the reports reviewed. The incidents follow a series of attacks and explosions involving ships in and near the strait in recent days, which Iran has linked to ships ignoring its warnings. The United Nations said on Saturday at least 25 seafarers had been killed around the strait since February.
keyFacts: Iran says three tankers hit naval mines
Iran says the ships caught fire
The claims have not been independently verified

articles.title: Israeli air strike kills senior Hamas commander in southern Gaza
articles.summary:
An Israeli air strike has killed a senior commander in Hamas's armed wing in southern Gaza, Al Jazeera reported. The Israeli military said it targeted a senior member of the group's military wing, according to Arab News and the Times of Israel.

Indian and regional outlets reported that Hamas confirmed the death of a Rafah-area commander, though the identity was not confirmed across the sources reviewed. The strike follows other Israeli strikes in Gaza this week, including one on Nasser Hospital that the Gaza health ministry said killed six people. Israel's military says it targets militants. Casualty figures from Sunday's strike were not confirmed in the reports reviewed.
keyFacts: The strike was in southern Gaza
Israel's military says it targeted a senior Hamas military figure
It follows deadly strikes earlier in the week

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh
articles.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition has said it intercepted two missiles and two drones over Riyadh, according to Al Jazeera. Arab News and Pakistan's Express Tribune reported the coalition also said it brought down drones over the kingdom's Eastern Province.

The coalition attributed the attacks to Yemen's Houthi movement, Arab News reported. Damage or casualties were not reported in the sources reviewed. The Houthis said on Saturday they had fired missiles at Saudi forces in Jazan, as fighting between the two sides has intensified over the past week. Al Jazeera's live coverage reported further drone interceptions later in the day.
keyFacts: Two missiles and two drones were intercepted over Riyadh, the coalition says
Drones were also downed over the Eastern Province
The coalition blames the Houthis

articles.title: Iraq's prime minister sacks nine officials over alleged oil smuggling
articles.summary:
Iraq's prime minister has dismissed nine officials over alleged oil smuggling in an area regarded as a stronghold of pro-Iran armed groups, according to Al Jazeera, The New Arab and Arab News.

Al Jazeera reported the probe concerns smuggling worth about $US30 million. Al Jazeera described the area as a stronghold of a powerful militia. The officials' names and the specific allegations against them were not detailed in the sources reviewed, and responses from the dismissed officials or the armed groups were not reported. The dismissals were announced on Saturday, local time, according to the reports.
keyFacts: Nine officials were dismissed
The alleged smuggling was in a pro-Iran group stronghold
Al Jazeera put the smuggling at about $US30 million

articles.title: Victorian Labor makes $1 billion surgery plan centrepiece of campaign launch
articles.summary:
Victorian Labor has made a plan to spend about $1 billion on surgery the main announcement of its state election campaign launch, AAP reported. Premier Jacinta Allan presented the pledge at the party's launch in Melbourne on Sunday, according to AAP and the ABC.

The ABC reported both major parties held launches on the same day, with Labor focused on health and the Coalition on youth crime. Deputy Premier Ben Carroll also addressed the Labor launch, according to reports. Full costings and timelines for the surgery plan were not detailed in the reports reviewed, and the Coalition's response to the pledge was not reported. Victorians vote on 28 November, and Labor has governed the state since 2014.
keyFacts: The surgery pledge is worth about $1 billion
It was announced at Labor's campaign launch
Both major parties launched their campaigns on 15 November

articles.title: Victorian Coalition pledges regional bootcamp prison for young offenders
articles.summary:
Victorian Opposition Leader Jess Wilson has announced a Coalition plan for a regional bootcamp-style prison for young offenders, the ABC reported. The facility would be at Dhurringile in northern Victoria, according to the ABC, and the plan was unveiled at the Coalition's campaign launch on Sunday.

AAP reported the bootcamp was a central announcement of the Liberal launch. Ms Wilson said she was taking nothing for granted, according to reports of the launch. Details of cost, capacity and opening date were not set out in the reports reviewed, and Labor's response to the plan was not reported. Victorians vote on 28 November.
keyFacts: The site proposed is Dhurringile
The plan targets young offenders
It was announced at the Coalition's campaign launch

articles.title: SpaceX catches Starship upper stage at launch tower for the first time
articles.summary:
SpaceX has caught the Starship spacecraft with its launch tower's mechanical arms after a flight around Earth, the first time it has recovered the vehicle's upper stage this way, according to Al Jazeera, the ABC and Space.com. The 15th Starship test flight launched from Starbase in Texas.

The Statesman and other outlets reported the ship completed about 14 orbits before returning. SpaceX has previously caught the Super Heavy booster with the tower, but earlier upper stages splashed down or were lost. The company says catching both stages is key to making the rocket fully reusable, which NASA is relying on for its planned crewed Moon landings.
keyFacts: It was Starship's 15th test flight
The upper stage was caught by the tower's arms
SpaceX had previously caught only the booster

articles.title: Netanyahu calls for unity government with Eisenkot, citing Iran threat
