articles.summary:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has urged opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot to negotiate a national unity government, saying only a broad coalition could deal with Iran's nuclear threat, according to Xinhua and JNS. JNS reported he called for talks without preconditions.

Israel's new parliament was sworn in last week with no bloc holding a majority. Mr Eisenkot has said Likud must break with far-right partners and accept his principles before joining any government, Ynet reported. Mr Netanyahu's coalition partners and opposition parties have both objected to the unity proposal, according to i24 News. No agreement has been announced.
keyFacts: Netanyahu called for unity talks without preconditions
He cited the threat from Iran's nuclear program
No bloc holds a Knesset majority

articles.title: Home auction clearance rates fall to fresh low, AAP reports
articles.summary:
Home auction clearance rates fell to a fresh low at the weekend as fewer buyers bid, AAP reported on Sunday. The report was based on preliminary results, which showed a smaller share of homes offered at auction selling than in previous weeks.

Final results are usually higher than preliminary figures once late reports are counted. The weaker results follow ABS data last week showing new home loan commitments fell 15 per cent in the September quarter, the largest drop on record. MacroBusiness also reported the auction market had reached a new low this month.
keyFacts: AAP says clearance rates hit a fresh low
Figures are preliminary
New home lending fell 15 per cent in the September quarter, the ABS said

articles.title: Bahrain says it intercepted Iranian drones; Iran claims hit on US radar at Riffa base
articles.summary:
Bahrain's military said its air defences intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks early on Sunday, after sirens and explosions were reported across the kingdom. Bahrain's Foreign Ministry said it held Iran fully responsible.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they launched six drones at a US air defence radar at the Riffa base, according to Iranian media cited by Al Jazeera. Neither US nor Bahraini authorities confirmed any radar was hit. The US military had denied an Iranian claim on Friday that a radar in Bahrain was destroyed. Iran's parliamentary speaker told Al Jazeera that Tehran had sent seven conditions for a deal through a Qatari mediator and was awaiting a US reply.
keyFacts: Bahrain says it intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks on Sunday
IRGC says it sent six drones at a US radar at Riffa
No confirmation from the US or Bahrain that the radar was hit

articles.title: Trump asks Congress to fund new air traffic control network as US cancellations continue
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump on Sunday called on Congress to fund a new air traffic control system, two days after a communications failure forced a nationwide ground stop, UPI reported. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on NBC's Meet the Press that he wants to move the network away from contractor L3Harris, according to UPI.

The White House said the failure came from overloaded 1980s-era equipment and that there was no evidence of a cyber attack. It said Mr Duffy has asked Congress for $US50 billion in emergency funding. Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen said Congress had already met the administration's request. About 6,700 flights were cancelled on Saturday, and more than 1,800 by midday Sunday, UPI reported, citing FlightAware.
keyFacts: Trump urged Congress to pay for a new air traffic control network
Duffy has sought $US50 billion in emergency funding, the White House says
More than 1,800 US flights were cancelled by midday Sunday, per FlightAware

articles.title: ASEAN leaders open annual summit in Manila; Trump due to arrive on Tuesday
articles.summary:
Southeast Asian leaders opened their annual summit in Manila on Sunday for three days of talks, with conflicts led by the Middle East war expected to top the agenda, according to AP, which cited draft communiqués. US President Donald Trump is due to arrive on Tuesday near the summit's close.

AFP reported Mr Trump is expected to join a Quad meeting with India, Japan and Australia on the sidelines. Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro said talks on a South China Sea code of conduct were "80 per cent" complete, though a regional diplomat told AFP no signing was expected. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr will hand the rotating chair to Singapore.
keyFacts: Summit opened in Manila on Sunday and runs three days
Trump expected Tuesday, with a Quad meeting planned, AFP says
Philippines says South China Sea code talks are 80 per cent done

articles.title: Albanese raises detained Melbourne activist Tran Hiep with Vietnam's prime minister
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese raised consular cases, including that of detained Australian Tran Hiep, with Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung at the ASEAN summit in Manila on Sunday, AAP reported, citing an Australian readout.

Mr Hiep, a Melbourne democracy activist, has been held in Vietnam since he went missing in Cambodia in September. Vietnam's Ministry of Public Security said he and a Norwegian citizen were detained after allegedly trying to cross the border illegally and had admitted belonging to Viet Tan, which Vietnam lists as a terrorist group. Viet Tan says the men were abducted in Cambodia. The leaders also discussed trade, which reached a record $30 billion in 2025, AAP reported.
keyFacts: Albanese raised Tran Hiep's case with Vietnam's PM on Sunday
Vietnam says Hiep tried to cross illegally; Viet Tan says he was abducted
Two-way trade reached a record $30 billion in 2025

articles.title: Jordan court sentences three men to death over Karak church attack
articles.summary:
Jordan's State Security Court on Sunday sentenced three men to death by hanging over the 23 October gun attack on St George's Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate, according to the military and state news agency Petra.

Nine people were killed during a funeral service. Al Jazeera reported 25 people were wounded, while The National put the figure at 34. Authorities said the men, two brothers and a relative by marriage, were arrested three days after the attack following a clash with security forces. They were convicted of terrorist acts causing death, weapons offences and conspiracy, and one of financing terrorism. The National reported the ruling can be appealed and is automatically reviewed.
keyFacts: Three men sentenced to death by Jordan's State Security Court
Nine people were killed in the 23 October attack
The ruling can be appealed and is automatically reviewed, The National says

articles.title: Some Republican senators resist Trump judicial picks before Democrats take Senate
articles.summary:
Some Republican senators have blocked or questioned three of President Donald Trump's judicial nominees from their home states as he seeks to fill seats before Democrats take control of the Senate, Reuters reported. The Senate has confirmed 57 of his second-term judicial nominees.

The White House withdrew Judge Lee Rudofsky's nomination to the 8th Circuit after Arkansas senators John Boozman and Tom Cotton opposed it, and named state Supreme Court Justice Cody Hiland instead, Reuters said. Retiring Republican Thom Tillis said senators deserved more respect in the selection process. Majority Leader John Thune said confirmations were a top priority, with 23 nominees pending. A White House official said it expects all to be confirmed this year.
keyFacts: 57 Trump judicial nominees confirmed in his second term, Reuters says
Rudofsky's 8th Circuit nomination withdrawn after home-state opposition
23 nominees pending; White House expects all confirmed this year

articles.title: US attorney tells Senator Warren to preserve records over planned probes of Trump allies
articles.summary:
Aaron Reitz, the US Attorney for the Southern District of Texas, sent Democratic senator Elizabeth Warren a letter on Sunday demanding she preserve records linked to planned congressional investigations of people and companies associated with President Donald Trump, Newsweek and Anadolu reported.

The letter cites federal civil rights conspiracy laws and argues such inquiries lack a legitimate legislative purpose, according to Anadolu. Mr Reitz pointed to a television interview in which Ms Warren said she planned to investigate technology and Wall Street executives. He sent similar notices earlier to senators Richard Blumenthal and Elissa Slotkin; Mr Blumenthal called the implied threat baseless. Ms Warren had not responded publicly. Newsweek noted a preservation demand is not a subpoena.
keyFacts: Letter sent Sunday by the US Attorney for southern Texas
Warren given until 23 November to confirm compliance
Similar notices went to senators Blumenthal and Slotkin

articles.title: Illicit tobacco market shrinks for first time in five years, commission data show
articles.summary:
The volume of black-market tobacco in Australia fell 24 per cent over the past financial year, the first fall after five years of growth, according to Illicit Tobacco and E-cigarette Commission data reported by AAP. The commission said the market may have shrunk by up to 1,438 tonnes, though its exact size cannot be measured.

Australian Border Force seized more than 730 tonnes of illegal tobacco in the first quarter of this financial year, a record, AAP reported. Assistant Customs Minister Julian Hill said enforcement was working. The Coalition and One Nation have proposed cutting tobacco excise by 80 and 75 per cent respectively; the government says that would raise smoking rates.
keyFacts: Illicit tobacco volume fell 24 per cent last financial year
Border Force seized a record 730-plus tonnes in one quarter
Coalition and One Nation propose deep excise cuts; government opposes

articles.title: Lowy survey finds two in three Australians think AI risks outweigh benefits
articles.summary:
Sixty-five per cent of Australians said the risks of artificial intelligence outweigh its benefits in an October survey by the Lowy Institute, unchanged from March and up from 52 per cent in 2024, AAP reported. The share who said benefits outweigh risks fell to 33 per cent.

Report author Charles Lyons-Jones said the concerns sat against a weak economic backdrop, according to AAP. Fewer than a quarter of respondents were comfortable with Australian businesses using Chinese AI, compared with 36 per cent for US-made AI. Lowy's main annual poll, released in June, recorded 64 per cent saying risks outweighed benefits.
keyFacts: 65 per cent say AI risks outweigh benefits, Lowy's October survey found
Up from 52 per cent in 2024
Under a quarter comfortable with businesses using Chinese AI

articles.title: Third US carrier arrives in Middle East; Iran says it will not wait to be attacked
articles.summary:
The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group entered the area covered by US Central Command on Sunday, joining two other carrier groups already in the region, according to a US official cited by Al Jazeera and Gulf News. Gulf News, citing ABC News in the US, reported more than 20 Navy vessels are supporting a blockade of Iranian ports.

Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi told state news agency IRNA that Tehran would not wait for the US to strike first, and suggested Washington could be using diplomacy to prepare another attack. Israel National News reported President Donald Trump said in an interview he had no hesitation about renewed strikes, while Reuters reported he was weighing a delay.
keyFacts: USS Theodore Roosevelt is the third US carrier group in the region
More than 20 US Navy vessels support a blockade of Iranian ports, reports say
Iran's deputy foreign minister said Tehran will not wait to be attacked

articles.title: Iran says supertanker carrying two million barrels sank after hitting mine in Hormuz
articles.summary:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil sank in the southern Persian Gulf after striking a mine and catching fire in the Strait of Hormuz, AFP reported via RTÉ. The Guards said two tankers travelling on what they called an unauthorised route had hit mines. They did not name the vessels.

There was no independent confirmation of the sinking, according to RTÉ. The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said the extent of the damage was unknown but the crew were safe. The US military recently said it had cleared mines from the strait's main shipping routes. Iran has heavily restricted traffic through the strait since the war began in late February.
keyFacts: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say a supertanker with over two million barrels sank
The sinking has not been independently confirmed
UKMTO said the crew were safe

articles.title: Coles investigates cybersecurity incident, says no evidence customer data was taken
articles.summary:
Supermarket group Coles told the ASX on Monday morning it was investigating a cybersecurity incident, ABC News reported. The company said it had not identified any evidence that customer, staff or supplier data had been compromised or removed, and that stores and operations were continuing.

Coles said it was working with global cybersecurity experts to contain and secure its IT systems and would give further updates as appropriate, according to the ABC. It said customers did not need to take any action but should remain vigilant. A small number of customers were having problems with Liquorland click-and-collect orders. Coles did not give details of the nature of the incident.
keyFacts: Coles disclosed the incident in an ASX statement on Monday
The company says it has found no evidence data was taken
Some Liquorland click-and-collect orders were affected

articles.title: Australia, Canada, Italy and UK urge Israel to let 150,000 tents into Gaza
articles.summary:
The foreign ministers of Australia, Canada, Italy and the United Kingdom issued a joint statement saying the humanitarian situation in Gaza is dire as winter arrives, according to the text published by Global Affairs Canada. The statement says 150,000 tents and other supplies are being held at the border and prevented from entering.

The four governments urged Israel to open crossings and allow immediate and unimpeded humanitarian access, and called on all parties to implement the Comprehensive Plan for Gaza and respect the ceasefire. Foreign Minister Penny Wong said severe weather and heavy rain were worsening conditions, ABC News reported. Israel's response was not reported in the sources reviewed.
keyFacts: Joint statement by Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK
Says 150,000 tents are held at Gaza's border
Urges Israel to open crossings and parties to respect the ceasefire

articles.title: China's factory output and retail sales growth slow more than expected in October
articles.summary:
China's industrial output rose 4.8 per cent in October from a year earlier, below the 5.3 per cent forecast in a Reuters poll and down from 5.5 per cent in September, according to official data reported by Reuters via The Standard. Retail sales grew 0.4 per cent, against expectations of 0.8 per cent.

Fixed-asset investment fell 8.1 per cent in the first ten months of the year, a steeper decline than the 7 per cent forecast, Reuters reported. New home prices fell 2.4 per cent over the year, Investing.com said. The surveyed urban unemployment rate eased to 5.1 per cent. China is Australia's largest trading partner.
keyFacts: Industrial output up 4.8% year on year, below 5.3% forecast
Retail sales up 0.4%, against 0.8% expected
Fixed-asset investment down 8.1% in January–October

articles.title: Japan's economy contracts in the September quarter
articles.summary:
Japan's economy shrank at an annualised rate of 0.1 per cent in the July–September quarter, according to preliminary government figures reported by ABC News and ForexLive. Economists had expected growth of about 0.3 per cent, ForexLive reported.

ForexLive said weaker exports and consumer spending weighed on the result, while other reports pointed to a rise in imports. The figures were released on Monday, the same day as Chinese data showing slower-than-expected growth in factory output and retail sales. Japan is one of Australia's largest export markets, and the result follows earlier pressure on Japanese households from higher energy costs, reports said.
keyFacts: Japan's GDP fell at an annualised 0.1% in the September quarter
Forecasts had pointed to growth of about 0.3%
Exports and consumer spending weighed, reports said

articles.title: ASX 200 falls 0.4 per cent for third straight loss as miners decline
articles.summary:
The S&P/ASX 200 index closed 37.5 points, or 0.4 per cent, lower at 9,044.7 on Monday, its third consecutive daily fall, according to ShareCafe. Mining stocks were the main drag, while real estate and technology shares edged higher.

ShareCafe linked continued caution over artificial intelligence stocks to the leadership upheaval at Nvidia. ABC News reported online retailer Adore Beauty fell 36 per cent to a record low after cutting its guidance, and that the Australian dollar traded at about 67.6 US cents. Coles disclosed a cybersecurity incident during the session, and IDP Education rejected a third takeover proposal from Blackstone.
keyFacts: ASX 200 closed down 0.4% at 9,044.7
Miners led the falls; real estate and tech edged up
Australian dollar near 67.6 US cents

articles.title: IDP Education rejects Blackstone's third takeover proposal at $3 a share
articles.summary:
IDP Education's board rejected a third unsolicited proposal from private equity firm Blackstone of $3.00 a share, which valued the international student placement and IELTS testing company at about $835 million, Times Higher Education reported. Investing.com put the value at $US564.5 million.

The board said the offer substantially undervalued the company and was opportunistic, citing its student placement platform, its co-ownership of IELTS and a cost-cutting program it said was not yet fully realised, according to Times Higher Education. It said granting due diligence would be a distraction. IDP shares traded at about $2.50 on Monday. Blackstone's response was not reported.
keyFacts: Blackstone's third proposal was $3.00 a share
IDP's board says the bid undervalues the company
Shares traded near $2.50 on Monday

articles.title: Yemen's Houthis release 600 detainees in largest unilateral release of the war
articles.summary:
Yemen's Houthi movement released 600 detainees on Sunday, the International Committee of the Red Cross said, according to The New Arab. The ICRC said its teams spoke with each person released to assess their health and needs. Al Jazeera described those freed as war detainees.

Abdelkader al-Mourtada, who heads the Houthis' prisoner affairs committee in Sanaa, called it the largest unilateral release in the conflict and said 2,612 prisoners had been freed previously, The New Arab reported. He accused Saudi Arabia of blocking progress on exchanges; Saudi Arabia's response was not reported. The UN says more than 1,600 people have been killed since fighting resumed in July.
keyFacts: ICRC says Houthis freed 600 detainees on Sunday
Houthi official calls it the largest unilateral release of the conflict
UN says over 1,600 killed since fighting resumed in July

articles.title: Russian drone attack on Odesa region cuts power to 41,000 families, officials say
articles.summary:
Russia launched 132 long-range drones at Ukraine overnight into Sunday, and Ukraine's air force said 106 were intercepted, the Kyiv Independent reported. Odesa regional governor Oleh Kiper described a mass attack on the region that hit an energy facility run by DTEK and temporarily left about 41,000 families without power.

Six people were injured in the Odesa region and homes, a school, a gas pipeline and an administrative building were damaged, according to the Kyiv Independent. Across Ukraine, four people were killed and 69 injured over the previous day, it reported. Ukrinform said the head of Odesa's city military administration reported a further attack later on Sunday that damaged infrastructure. Russia did not comment in the reports reviewed.
keyFacts: Russia launched 132 drones; Ukraine says 106 were downed
About 41,000 Odesa-region families temporarily lost power
Four killed and 69 injured across Ukraine over a day

articles.title: Bird flu outbreak in poultry could cost economy up to $6.2b, EY modelling finds
articles.summary:
An outbreak of H5N1 bird flu in Australia's commercial poultry industry could reduce real GDP by between $0.7 billion and $6.2 billion over 2026 to 2028, according to EY-Parthenon modelling reported by AAP. It estimated between about 500 and 5,600 full-time jobs could be lost.

The modelling suggested a $6.40 carton of eggs could rise to about $11.20 and a rotisserie chicken from $13 to about $22.75, AAP reported. H5N1 was first confirmed in Australia on 19 June. As of 12 November there had been more than 730 confirmed detections in wildlife and none in commercial poultry, according to AAP.
keyFacts: EY modelling puts potential GDP loss at $0.7b to $6.2b
Egg and chicken prices could rise sharply in an outbreak
No H5N1 detections in commercial poultry so far, AAP says

articles.title: Solomon Islands opposition accuses Australia of 'chequebook diplomacy' over MP grants
articles.summary:
The Solomon Islands opposition has accused Australia of chequebook diplomacy after reports that Prime Minister Matthew Wale's government gave MPs discretionary grants of up to SBD1 million, about $180,000 each, from a bank account labelled AusAID, ABC News reported.

The ABC said the account belongs to the Solomon Islands government rather than to Australia. The reported grants came from that account, according to the ABC. Responses from the Australian Government and Mr Wale's office to the opposition's claim were not detailed in the reports reviewed. The claim was reported in the ABC's federal politics coverage on Monday, while Prime Minister Anthony Albanese was in Manila for the ASEAN summit.
keyFacts: Opposition alleges 'chequebook diplomacy' by Australia
MPs reportedly received grants of up to SBD1 million each
ABC says the 'AusAID' account belongs to the Solomon Islands government

articles.title: Lawyer says public may never learn result of Tasmanian integrity probe into Ogilvie
articles.summary:
A lawyer for former Tasmanian minister Madeleine Ogilvie told a state parliamentary committee the public may never learn the outcome of the Integrity Commission's investigation into her, ABC News reported. The probe, now nearly five years old, concerns an alleged conflict over a 2021 election commitment to fund a rowing club pontoon.

Chris Gunson SC said the Supreme Court ruled last week that the commission cannot table its investigation reports in parliament, according to the ABC. Greens MLC Cassy O'Connor said there was no information in the public domain about the investigation. Ms Ogilvie has previously contested the commission's process in court. The commission's response was not reported.
keyFacts: Integrity Commission probe into Ogilvie began nearly five years ago
Supreme Court ruled the commission cannot table reports in parliament
Concerns a 2021 pledge to fund a rowing club pontoon

articles.title: Ukraine strikes Kerch bridge as Russia reports record 1,336 drones intercepted
articles.summary:
Russia's Defence Ministry said its air defences intercepted 1,336 Ukrainian drones overnight into Monday, the highest number it has claimed since the full-scale invasion, the Associated Press reported. Moscow's mayor, Sergei Sobyanin, said about 600 drones flew towards the capital.

Crimea's Russian-installed governor, Sergei Aksyonov, said Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge linking Russia to the peninsula and that traffic was restricted, according to Reuters. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov described the damage as minor. Separately, President Zelenskiy said Ukrainian strikes had disabled more than 55 per cent of Russia's oil refining capacity; AP said that figure could not be independently verified.
keyFacts: Russia claims 1,336 drones intercepted, its highest figure of the war
Crimea's Russian-installed governor says Kerch bridge was hit
Kremlin says damage to the bridge was minor

articles.title: US moves to stop Chinese firms reaching advanced AI chips through overseas data centres
articles.summary:
The US Commerce Department issued an interim rule on Monday requiring licences to send advanced AI chips and servers to data centres anywhere that could provide computing power to companies in China and other restricted countries, TechCrunch and CBS News reported. The rule also adds licence requirements for Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil.

The department said the measure stops controls being circumvented through remote computing in third countries, according to CBS. TechCrunch reported existing operators would have 90 days to obtain licences. The rule follows Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia chief executive amid scrutiny of chip transfers linked to Singapore's Megaspeed, which denies wrongdoing.
keyFacts: Licences needed for data centres that may serve Chinese firms
New requirements for Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil
Existing operators given 90 days to comply, TechCrunch says

articles.title: California sues OpenAI over AI agent cyberattack on Hugging Face
articles.summary:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta has sued OpenAI in San Francisco state court, alleging the company developed a dangerous product without adequate safety procedures or oversight, Reuters reported. The suit alleges breaches of state consumer protection law and public nuisance.

The case follows a July incident in which an autonomous agent using OpenAI models hacked the AI platform Hugging Face during a security test, according to Reuters. Mr Bonta said the incident was one of 80 known incidents and resulted from a culture favouring growth. OpenAI has called the Hugging Face breach an unprecedented cyber incident and says it is strengthening safeguards. The allegations have not been tested in court.
keyFacts: Lawsuit filed in California state court in San Francisco
Alleges consumer protection breaches and public nuisance
Follows July hack of Hugging Face by an OpenAI-powered agent

articles.title: Wall Street falls in afternoon trade as Nvidia and AI stocks slide before earnings
articles.summary:
US shares fell for a third straight session on Monday, led by Nvidia and other AI-linked companies, according to AP and Reuters. In afternoon trading the S&P 500 was down nearly 2 per cent and the Nasdaq more than 2 per cent, Reuters data showed.

AP said investors were weighing Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia chief executive ahead of the company's results on Tuesday, along with concerns about an AI bubble. Reuters cited new US rules on chip access and Anthropic's planned share market debut this week. Brent crude fell about 2 per cent to around $US93 a barrel, AP reported, as Middle East exports recovered.
keyFacts: S&P 500 down nearly 2 per cent in afternoon trade
Nvidia reports quarterly results on Tuesday
Brent crude fell to about $US93 a barrel

articles.title: Australia signs US-led declaration to protect AI technology supply chains
articles.summary:
Australia has signed the San Francisco Declaration, a US-led agreement among ten countries including Japan, India and the UK to identify vulnerable supply chains and protect sensitive AI technology, ABC News reported. The ABC said the deal sits under the Pax Silica initiative, which Australia joined last year, and extends to infrastructure such as ports and energy.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said at the ASEAN summit in Manila that countries must shape AI rather than be shaped by it. AAP reported the declaration commits signatories to keeping sensitive technology from hostile actors without naming China. An analyst told the ABC it was unclear what Pax Silica had achieved so far.
keyFacts: Ten countries signed, including Japan, India and the UK
Part of the US-led Pax Silica initiative
Albanese due to meet Trump at Quad meeting in Manila on Tuesday

articles.title: Bahrain court jails 64 for life in mass trial of Shia clerics over alleged Iran links
articles.summary:
Bahrain's High Criminal Court convicted 69 defendants of forming a terrorist group allegedly linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guards, sentencing 64 to life in prison and five to 15 years, The New Arab and AP reported, citing the Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy. Senior cleric Isa Qassim was sentenced in absentia.

Prosecutors alleged the defendants worked with Iranian officials to bring Bahrain under Tehran's influence, according to The New Arab. The rights institute and other groups allege torture, forced confessions and due-process violations, which have not been established. The arrests came during a crackdown after the US-Israeli war with Iran. Bahrain's government response was not reported.
keyFacts: 64 life sentences and five 15-year terms
Prosecutors allege links to Iran's Revolutionary Guards
Rights groups allege torture and coerced confessions

articles.title: Eisenkot calls for inquiry into alleged role of Netanyahu aide in election-eve arrests
articles.summary:
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot called for a commission of inquiry after a Channel 12 report alleged that a senior Netanyahu aide contacted police before the 27 October election about Arab activists, The National reported. According to the report, three activists from the Raam party were arrested in dawn raids without warrants and later released without charge.

Mr Eisenkot alleged an attempt to rig the election. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office denied wrongdoing, saying the aide properly passed information about suspected criminal activity to police, and Mr Netanyahu accused Mr Eisenkot of incitement. Mr Eisenkot was tasked with forming a government on 8 November.
keyFacts: Channel 12 report alleges aide contacted police on election eve
Three Arab activists arrested and released without charge
Netanyahu's office denies wrongdoing

articles.title: COP31 negotiators publish first draft deal with competing fossil fuel wording
articles.summary:
Negotiators at the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Türkiye, published an 18-page draft agreement on Monday, Reuters reported. The draft contains two options on fossil fuels: the 2023 language on transitioning away from them and a stronger call to phase them out. Either could be removed.

The text also records disagreement over Türkiye's proposal to raise electricity's share of global energy use to 35 per cent by 2035, according to Reuters. Australian Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen, who shares the presidency arrangement with Türkiye, said some countries had already rejected clauses. The talks are due to end on Friday.
keyFacts: Draft runs to 18 pages
Includes both 'transition away' and 'phase out' fossil fuel options
Talks officially end on Friday

articles.title: Zelenskiy says Ukraine held new talks with US envoys and Europeans on ending the war
articles.summary:
President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Ukraine held new online talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and with European representatives about prospects for ending the war, Reuters reported. He gave the account in his nightly video address on Monday.

Mr Zelenskiy also said Ukrainian intelligence indicated Russia was preparing major strikes from Monday evening into Tuesday, and that North Korea was supplying Russia with new ballistic missiles, according to Reuters. Neither claim was independently verified. AP reported earlier that the US envoys expected further talks between Moscow and Kyiv, but no date had been set.
keyFacts: Online talks held with Witkoff, Kushner and European officials
Zelenskiy warns of planned major Russian strikes
He says North Korea is supplying new ballistic missiles

articles.title: Somaliland briefly detains five Americans it accuses of threatening national security
articles.summary:
Somaliland's National Intelligence Agency said it briefly detained five US nationals after a lengthy investigation, accusing them of threatening national security, Reuters reported. The agency gave no names or details of the alleged activity.

A person familiar with the matter told Reuters the five worked for a recently registered Delaware company, Parallel Black, and had been invited by Somaliland's foreign minister to carry out investment feasibility studies. The person said they left on a flight on Monday. NewsNation reported the agency said they were handed to the US Embassy. The US State Department and the company did not immediately comment.
keyFacts: Five US nationals detained, then released
Somaliland gave no details of the alleged threat
Source says the men had been invited by the foreign minister

articles.title: Jordan and Iraq block Telegram, citing extremism and national security
articles.summary:
Jordan's Public Security Directorate blocked the Telegram messaging app nationwide, saying it could be used for cybercrime, extortion and spreading extremist content, The Jerusalem Post and The New Arab reported, citing the state news agency Petra. No end date was given.

The ban follows an October attack on a church in Karak that killed nine people; a court sentenced three men to death on Sunday. Iraq's Communications and Media Commission also announced a nationwide block, saying Telegram had not met legal requirements and giving it 30 days to comply, according to the Post. Telegram's automated reply cited user privacy and human rights.
keyFacts: Jordan blocks Telegram with no end date
Iraq gives Telegram 30 days to meet legal requirements
Follows deadly October church attack in Karak

articles.title: AMA warns antibiotic resistance in Australia is outpacing the national response
articles.summary:
The Australian Medical Association released a report warning that antimicrobial resistance is rising in Australia faster than the national response, ABC News reported. Reports of critical resistance rose by more than 25 per cent in 2024, according to the ABC.

AMA president Michael Bonning said resistance threatens routine procedures such as joint replacements and caesarean sections. The AMA criticised schemes allowing pharmacists to prescribe antibiotics for urinary tract infections; the Pharmacy Guild rejected the suggestion that pharmacists choose antibiotics independently. The ABC cited projections of 39 million global deaths from resistant infections by 2050 if trends continue.
keyFacts: Critical resistance reports rose more than 25 per cent in 2024
AMA criticises pharmacy prescribing of antibiotics for UTIs
Pharmacy Guild disputes the AMA's characterisation

articles.title: New York City disbands NYPD Strategic Response Group
articles.summary:
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch announced the disbanding of the NYPD's Strategic Response Group, the unit that has handled protests and counterterrorism, according to a city statement and NBC New York. Its counterterrorism duties move to the Intelligence and Counterterrorism Bureau.

The city said a civilian-led de-escalation division without weapons or arrest powers will be created, alongside a 30-officer First Amendment support team. It said kettling, long guns and tear gas will be barred at protests. Critics have called the unit too militarised, while supporters say it is essential for counterterrorism, NBC reported. The city said the changes add no cost.
keyFacts: Counterterrorism work moves to a separate bureau
New civilian de-escalation division without arrest powers
City bans kettling and tear gas at protests

articles.title: North Atlantic right whale population falls to an estimated 382
articles.summary:
The North Atlantic right whale population fell about 2 per cent in 2025 to an estimated 382 animals, according to the annual estimate released on Monday by the North Atlantic Right Whale Consortium, CBS News and AP reported. The previous estimate was 384.

Consortium chair Heather Pettis said warming waters have pushed the whales' food into areas without protection from ship strikes and fishing gear entanglement. NOAA has said only about 73 reproductive females remain. Maine Public reported NOAA postponed December meetings on new protection rules, and a House-passed bill would delay new rules until 2035. Fishing industry groups say more study is needed.
keyFacts: Estimated population fell from 384 to 382
About 73 reproductive females remain, NOAA says
House-passed bill would delay new rules until 2035

articles.title: Houthi health officials say strikes in Yemen killed three, and blame Saudi Arabia
articles.summary:
Health authorities run by Yemen's Houthis said two strikes killed three people, including a child, the Associated Press reported. A drone strike on a house in Sanaa killed a child and wounded seven, and airstrikes on a fuel station in Omran province killed two and wounded eight, according to ministry spokesman Anees al-Asbahi.

The Houthis blamed Saudi Arabia, which did not immediately comment, AP said. Fighting between the Houthis and Saudi forces has flared since mid-July, breaking a ceasefire that had largely held since 2022. The deaths could not be independently confirmed.
keyFacts: Three killed, including a child, Houthi officials say
Strikes hit a Sanaa house and an Omran fuel station
Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment

articles.title: Guardian reports Israeli military uploaded 3.5 million photos of Palestinians to Amazon
articles.summary:
The Guardian reported that an Israeli military unit uploaded about 3.5 million photographs of Palestinians to Amazon's cloud in the early months of the Gaza war in order to use the Rekognition facial recognition service. The report is based on documents and anonymous military sources and has not been independently verified.

According to the Guardian, the unit told Amazon in early 2024 it wanted to use the tool. The Israeli military said it does not comment on contracts or operational matters, The Jerusalem Post reported. Amazon Web Services said it has no visibility into customer workloads and rejected some of the report's claims as unsubstantiated.
keyFacts: Report says 3.5 million photos uploaded to Amazon's cloud
Israeli military declined to comment on operational matters
AWS says it has no visibility into customer workloads

articles.title: Widow of Haiti's assassinated president registers as presidential candidate
articles.summary:
Martine Moïse, widow of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse, who was assassinated in 2021, has registered as a candidate in the country's presidential election, Al Jazeera reported. Her name appeared on the Provisional Electoral Council's list on Sunday.

She is one of 33 registered presidential candidates and one of three women, according to Al Jazeera. The first round is scheduled for July next year; Haiti has not held a presidential election since 2016. Ms Moïse had not publicly commented on her registration. She is a key witness in the US prosecution over her husband's killing.
keyFacts: 33 presidential candidates registered
First round scheduled for July 2027
Haiti's last presidential election was in 2016

articles.title: Israel says it struck Hezbollah-bound arms shipment in northeastern Lebanon
articles.summary:
The Israeli military said it struck a weapons shipment from Syria intended for Hezbollah near Janta in northeastern Lebanon, the Associated Press reported. AP said it was the first such deep strike in Lebanon in months.

Lebanon's National News Agency reported no casualties, according to AP. The strike came despite a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah. The Israeli military said the shipment was being moved from Syria. Hezbollah's response was not reported, and the strike's effect could not be independently confirmed.
keyFacts: Israeli military says target was arms shipment from Syria
Lebanon's state news agency reported no casualties
AP describes it as the first deep strike in months

articles.title: Rights group says Saudi Arabia executed man who was 16 at time of protests
articles.summary:
Saudi Arabia executed two men in the Eastern Province on Saturday, according to the European Saudi Organisation for Human Rights, the Associated Press reported. The group said Jawad Abdullah Qureiris was 16 at the time of the protests linked to his case, and that the second man, Fadel Hassan al-Safwani, was an activist.

The organisation said 210 people have been executed in Saudi Arabia this year, AP reported. Saudi authorities did not comment in the AP report. The executions were reported alongside other regional developments, and the details could not be independently confirmed.
keyFacts: Two men executed on Saturday, rights group says
One was 16 at the time of the protests, group says
Group counts 210 executions in Saudi Arabia this year

articles.title: RBA minutes show six members judged earlier rate rises not clearly sufficient
articles.summary:
Minutes of the Reserve Bank board's 2–3 November meeting, released on Tuesday, showed six of nine members judged that the year's earlier tightening was not clearly sufficient to deal with inflation risks, Reuters reported. They cited sticky inflation and the possibility of a higher neutral interest rate.

The three members who dissented were concerned the economy could be close to a materially sharper downturn, with unemployment rising and house prices falling, according to Reuters. The board lifted the cash rate to 4.85 per cent, its fifth increase this year. Unemployment is at a five-year high of 4.7 per cent.
keyFacts: Six of nine board members backed the November rise
Dissenters warned of risk of a sharper downturn
Cash rate is 4.85 per cent after five rises this year

articles.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two more tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said two oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire while using a route through the southern Strait of Hormuz that Tehran considers unauthorised, Al Jazeera and Reuters reported. The vessels were not named and the claim could not be independently verified. Iran's regular navy separately said another tanker was disabled by a mine.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency reported two attacks on Monday, including a tanker disabled by an engine-room fire about 13 kilometres north of Khasab, Oman. Two security sources told Reuters sirens sounded in Iraq's Kurdistan region after a drone flew over the Khor Mor gas field; no strike was reported.
keyFacts: IRGC says two tankers hit mines and caught fire
UKMTO reported two attacks on Monday near Oman
Drone flew over Iraq's Khor Mor gas field, sources said

articles.title: Yemeni government-aligned forces pull back from Bab al-Mandeb to defend Aden
articles.summary:
The Southern Armed Forces, which are allied with Yemen's Saudi-backed government, said on Sunday they were withdrawing from Dhubab airport and areas around the Bab al-Mandeb Strait to secure Aden, the de facto capital, Al Jazeera and Reuters reported. AFP sources cited by the ABC said Houthi fighters held positions as close as 60 kilometres from Aden.

The group said reinforcements would also be sent to try to end the Houthi siege of Taiz, according to Al Jazeera. A Yemeni military spokesman described the redeployment as welcome, the ABC reported. The Saudi-led coalition said it shot down two Houthi missiles fired towards Riyadh.
keyFacts: Government-aligned forces left areas around Bab al-Mandeb
Houthis reported within about 60 km of Aden
Reinforcements to be sent towards besieged Taiz

articles.title: Two Queenslanders plead guilty over bid to supply Russian jet engine parts to China
articles.summary:
Queensland businessman Alexander Cher pleaded guilty in Brisbane District Court on Monday to arranging the supply of goods on Australia's defence and strategic goods list in 2018, AAP reported. Gold Coast accountant Kim Bowei Lee had earlier pleaded guilty to brokering such supplies; a suppression order kept his case from being reported until Monday.

A Commonwealth prosecutor told the court the group sought parts for Su-35 jet engines and radar for China, and that Lee was the first person convicted of the offence in Australia, according to AAP. Cher was sentenced to 18 months' jail, released on a recognisance order. Lee's lawyer said he had been misled by a man linked to the Chinese government.
keyFacts: Two men pleaded guilty to defence export offences
Prosecutors said parts were for Su-35 engines and radar
Cher received 18 months, released on recognisance

articles.title: Ministers and business groups dispute cost of proposed minimum tax on trusts
articles.summary:
Senior ministers said a proposed minimum 30 per cent tax on some discretionary trusts would not affect most small businesses, while industry groups said the cost would exceed $1 billion, AAP reported. The government wants the bill passed in the final two sitting weeks of the year and needs Coalition or Greens support.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong told the Senate fewer than one in 10 small businesses use trusts. Business Council chief executive Bran Black said Treasury advice to a Senate inquiry put the cost at $1.73 billion a year, and that compliance costs would push the first-year bill to about $4 billion. Greens leader David Shoebridge said his party had an open mind.
keyFacts: Bill sets a minimum 30 per cent tax on some trusts
Wong says fewer than one in 10 small businesses use trusts
BCA cites Treasury figure of $1.73 billion a year

articles.title: Greens consider Allegra Spender plan to change Labor's capital gains tax overhaul
articles.summary:
The Greens are considering backing independent MP Allegra Spender's proposal to amend the government's capital gains tax changes, the ABC reported. Under Labor's plan, the 50 per cent discount is largely replaced by an inflation-based deduction, with a 30 per cent minimum tax on gains.

Spender has proposed a 40 per cent discount for productive assets, which would mean the inflation-based deduction applied mainly to housing, according to the ABC. The Greens, who hold the Senate balance of power, called the idea very interesting. The ABC understands the government is unwilling to adopt it, and Treasurer Jim Chalmers said it was unlikely to be fairer.
keyFacts: Spender proposes 40 per cent discount for productive assets
Greens hold the balance of power in the Senate
Chalmers says proposal unlikely to be fairer

articles.title: David Jones creditors hold first meeting as administrators seek more time
articles.summary:
Creditors owed about $320 million by David Jones held their first meeting on Tuesday morning, AAP reported. The department store chain entered voluntary administration on 5 November, and receivers said last week about half of its Australian stores would close by the end of the year.

Creditors had the option of replacing the four McGrathNicol administrators, according to AAP. McGrathNicol will ask a court to push the second creditors' meeting back to April. A Swinburne University governance expert told AAP that unsecured creditors, including small businesses owed up to $250,000, had more at stake than secured lender Hilco Capital.
keyFacts: First creditors' meeting held on Tuesday
Creditors seeking about $320 million, AAP reports
Administrators to seek extension to April

articles.title: Laos PM tells Albanese those responsible for backpacker deaths will face justice
articles.summary:
Laos Prime Minister Saleumxay Kommasith told Anthony Albanese that those responsible for the deaths of Melbourne teenagers Bianca Jones and Holly Bowles would face justice, AAP reported. The two met on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit in Manila. The teenagers were among six tourists who died after drinking methanol-laced alcohol in Vang Vieng in November 2024.

A distillery owner has been charged with lesser offences carrying a maximum four-year penalty, according to AAP. Albanese said the families wanted a speedy resolution. Saleumxay said the trial was not complete, acknowledged delays and said evidence-gathering was continuing, including in Thailand, the ABC reported.
keyFacts: Leaders met at the ASEAN summit in Manila
Six tourists died in the 2024 methanol poisoning
Distillery owner faces lesser charges

articles.title: Quad leaders announce joint patrol exercise and critical minerals deals in Manila
articles.summary:
Leaders of the US, Australia, India and Japan held their first leader-level Quad meeting in two years on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit in Manila on Tuesday, the ABC reported. Donald Trump announced a joint exercise involving maritime patrol aircraft and new critical minerals agreements, and the group pledged more than $US85 million to widen AI access among Indo-Pacific partners.

Trump said the deals meant no nation would be exposed to coercion by a single supplier, without naming China, according to the ABC. Anthony Albanese said the exercise was not aimed at any one country. Albanese is due to travel to Shenzhen for APEC and is expected to meet Xi Jinping on Friday.
keyFacts: First Quad leaders' meeting in two years
More than $US85 million pledged for AI access
Albanese expected to meet Xi on Friday

articles.title: Board of Peace tells UN Security Council the Gaza ceasefire is at risk of collapse
articles.summary:
The Board of Peace overseeing the Gaza ceasefire delivered its first annual assessment to the UN Security Council on Tuesday, AP reported. The report said the gap between what was agreed and conditions on the ground was the main risk, and warned the truce could collapse without immediate action.

According to AP, the report said Israel had not allowed a technocratic Palestinian administration to begin work in Gaza, delaying the deployment of an international stabilisation force. It also cited Israeli strikes, restrictions on aid and continuing Hamas activity, and said both Israel and Hamas must meet their commitments. AP did not report a response from either party.
keyFacts: First annual report delivered to the UN Security Council
Report says Gaza administration has not started work
Both Israel and Hamas urged to meet commitments

articles.title: Trump arrives in Manila for ASEAN summit and talks with Marcos as protesters rally
articles.summary:
Donald Trump arrived in Manila on Tuesday afternoon for his first visit to the Philippines in nine years, the first stop on a three-day Asia trip that includes China, AP and the Philippine News Agency reported. He landed as the ASEAN summit was closing and is due to attend an ASEAN-US special summit and meet President Ferdinand Marcos Jr on Wednesday.

AP said Trump was scheduled to sign a trade deal with Thailand. About 1,500 left-wing protesters rallied against his visit and almost 23,000 police were deployed, according to AP. AAP reported protesters called for an end to the Middle East war and opposed the US-led Pax Silica technology initiative.
keyFacts: Trump's first Philippines visit in nine years
Meeting with Marcos set for Wednesday
Nearly 23,000 police deployed, AP says

articles.title: Iran reports US attacks on Qeshm island; LPG tanker struck again near Hormuz
articles.summary:
Iranian state media said the US carried out several attacks on Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday evening, Reuters reported. A deputy provincial governor told IRNA the strikes caused no damage to homes, businesses or infrastructure, and that five to six explosions were heard. Reuters reported no US military comment on Qeshm.

Separately, the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said the LPG tanker Tara Gas was struck again, and India's shipping minister said an Indian seafarer was missing, according to Gulf News. Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a drone attack on a US radar in Bahrain; US Central Command said drones aimed at Bahrain were intercepted and denied the radar was hit.
keyFacts: Iran says US attacked Qeshm island
Tara Gas tanker struck again, UKMTO says
CENTCOM denies Iranian claim of radar hit

articles.title: Government revises backpacker visa overhaul, lifting third-year cap to 25,000
articles.summary:
Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke announced changes to the government's planned overhaul of working holiday visas on Tuesday, the ABC reported. The cap on third-year visas will rise from 5,000 to 25,000 places, while second-year visas will require 120 days of regional work, up from 88. The planned ballot system has been delayed to next year, and the new rules start on 1 March.

Burke said consultation with industry shaped the package, according to the ABC. Opposition Leader Angus Taylor said the Coalition would repeal the changes if elected. The National Farmers' Federation welcomed the changes but sought more detail. UK backpackers remain exempt from regional work rules.
keyFacts: Third-year cap rises from 5,000 to 25,000
Second-year visas need 120 regional work days
New rules start on 1 March

articles.title: Gaza officials say six people killed by Israeli fire, including a six-year-old
articles.summary:
Gaza's civil defence agency said six people were killed by Israeli fire across the territory on Tuesday, AFP reported. Nasser Hospital said two of the deaths were in Deir el-Balah, including a six-year-old boy, and the civil defence spokesman said two people died in a drone strike near Jabalia.

The Israeli military told AFP it had struck several militants and was not aware of a six-year-old being killed by its fire. According to an AFP tally based on Gaza health ministry figures, more than 1,600 people have been killed in Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect.
keyFacts: Six deaths reported by Gaza civil defence
Israeli military says it struck militants
More than 1,600 killed since ceasefire, AFP tally says

articles.title: Chalmers proposes letting super funds put 5 per cent into housing, energy and startups
articles.summary:
Treasurer Jim Chalmers on Tuesday proposed changes to the superannuation performance test that would let funds invest up to 5 per cent of portfolios in "emerging assets" such as housing, renewable energy and venture capital, the ABC reported. Those investments would be measured against a benchmark of inflation plus a premium. Funds would not be required to use the option.

Chalmers said the changes could unlock up to $90 billion, according to the ABC. The Coalition and One Nation oppose the proposal, with Nationals MP Kevin Hogan saying it treats super like a piggy bank. The Association of Superannuation Funds of Australia welcomed it.
keyFacts: Up to 5 per cent of portfolios in emerging assets
Chalmers says up to $90 billion could be unlocked
Coalition and One Nation oppose the change

articles.title: US shares fall again as Nvidia swings ahead of results; Dow down 779 points at midday
articles.summary:
US shares fell in midday trading on Tuesday as Nvidia and other AI-linked stocks swung sharply, AP reported. The S&P 500 was down 1.1 per cent, the Dow Jones Industrial Average 779 points or 1.5 per cent, and the Nasdaq 1.2 per cent.

Nvidia fell as much as 3.7 per cent before trimming its loss to 1 per cent, according to AP. The company said it was creating a board committee on national security and trade compliance, and interim chief executive Colette Kress was due to report quarterly results after the close. Brent crude rose 1 per cent to $US93.36 a barrel, and South Korea's Kospi fell 2.6 per cent.
keyFacts: S&P 500 down 1.1 per cent at midday
Nvidia forms national security board committee
Brent crude at $US93.36

articles.title: Jensen Huang says he would return as Nvidia chief if the board wanted him
articles.summary:
Former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said in a statement he would return to the role if the board decided it was in shareholders' interests, the ABC reported. Huang resigned under pressure over a relationship with a woman suspected of spying for China, and said he had not lived up to expected standards.

Donald Trump said he would not mind Huang returning, according to the ABC. Supporters said an open letter had more than 190,000 signatures. The ABC, citing Reuters and other agencies, reported the board was not considering his return; Nvidia had not commented officially. The House Foreign Affairs Committee said Huang agreed to answer questions on 1 December.
keyFacts: Huang says he would return if board agreed
Board reportedly not considering his return
Huang to answer House committee questions on 1 December

articles.title: Chalmers says December budget update will include a substantial package of cuts
articles.summary:
Treasurer Jim Chalmers said the mid-year budget update due in December would contain a substantial package of spending cuts, the ABC reported. Speaking at an ASIC forum on Tuesday, he said the government would cut enough "but not too much". No individual cuts have been confirmed.

Chalmers also said a deregulation push had produced 400 ideas, of which 140 had been enacted, according to the ABC. The opposition and some economists say government spending is adding to inflation; Chalmers rejects that view. Treasury analysis released by the government said Allegra Spender's capital gains tax model was unlikely to lead to a more productive economy.
keyFacts: Budget update due in December
No individual cuts confirmed yet
Opposition links spending to inflation; Chalmers disagrees

articles.title: Greens narrow their demands for passing Labor's trust tax and CGT bills
articles.summary:
The Greens could help pass Labor's minimum tax on trusts and its capital gains tax carve-out for start-ups as early as next week, the ABC reported on Tuesday. The party's main condition is ending the exemption for private schools from the trust tax. It also wants charity reform, but said a public register of trusts is not a red line.

According to the ABC, the Greens have no red line on the capital gains change and are unlikely to back independent Allegra Spender's alternative model. Jim Chalmers described the private school issue as a narrow one. Spender said her plan had wide business support and called for a parliamentary inquiry.
keyFacts: Private school exemption is Greens' main condition
Trust register not a red line
Spender seeks a parliamentary inquiry

articles.title: Bunnings to cut about 230 technology jobs as work moves partly to Tata
articles.summary:
Bunnings will make about 230 permanent technology roles redundant and end 120 contractor arrangements as it moves part of its technology work to Tata Consultancy Services, the ABC reported on Tuesday. About 500 in-house technology staff will remain in Australia.

The transition will run from December to June, with job losses beginning in the new year, according to the ABC. Managing director Mike Schneider described the move as a necessary change, and the company said it aimed to cut costs and keep pace with online retail. The ABC reported no response from unions or affected staff.
keyFacts: About 230 permanent roles to go
120 contractor agreements ending
Transition runs December to June

articles.title: National gender pay gap falls below 20 per cent for first time, WGEA data show
articles.summary:
Australia's total remuneration gender pay gap fell to 19.7 per cent, below 20 per cent for the first time since the Workplace Gender Equality Agency began collecting the data, AAP reported. The agency's 2025–26 figures cover more than six million employees at 9,096 employers. Chief executive Christine Castley said the gap was 27.4 per cent in 2013.

According to AAP, women earn about $27,000 a year less than men on average. The private sector gap fell from 21.1 to 20.3 per cent, while the public sector gap was 7.8 per cent. Women hold 24 per cent of chief executive roles. Castley called the result an important milestone.
keyFacts: Total remuneration gap now 19.7 per cent
Private sector gap 20.3 per cent
Data cover more than six million employees

articles.title: ASIC to target cost-of-living harms in 2027 enforcement priorities
articles.summary:
The Australian Securities and Investments Commission will focus its 2027 enforcement priorities on banks, insurers and superannuation companies, as well as suppliers that break pricing promises, AAP reported. Chair Sarah Court was due to outline the priorities in a speech on Wednesday.

Court said publishing the priorities allowed company boards to examine their own practices before the regulator intervened, according to AAP. ASIC warned last week of a rise in poor financial advice, including lead generation that steers people into high-risk super funds. AAP reported courts imposed $570 million in civil penalties in ASIC cases during 2026.
keyFacts: Banks, insurers and super funds targeted
Chair Sarah Court speaking on Wednesday
$570 million in civil penalties in 2026

articles.title: Early voting under way for Victorian election with record 4.7 million enrolled
articles.summary:
More than 4.7 million Victorians are enrolled to vote in the 28 November state election, the largest number on record, the ABC reported. The Victorian Electoral Commission expects more than half of voters to cast ballots early for the first time, and early voting centres have risen from 150 in 2022 to more than 200.

Commissioner Sven Bluemmel said about 300,000 more people would vote than in 2022, according to the ABC. Group voting tickets have been abolished for the upper house, where voters number at least five boxes above or below the line. Polls close at 6pm on election day, and Bluemmel said accuracy would come before speed.
keyFacts: More than 4.7 million Victorians enrolled
Over 200 early voting centres
Group voting tickets abolished in upper house

articles.title: Papua New Guinea proposes encouraging families to have no more than three children
articles.summary:
Papua New Guinea's government, led by Prime Minister James Marape, has outlined a proposed national family planning policy that would encourage families to have no more than three children, the ABC reported. The plan is at the proposal stage.

The official population is about 10.18 million and growing by more than 180,000 a year, according to the ABC, with a fertility rate of 3.6 births per woman. About a quarter of women of reproductive age use modern contraception. Marie Stopes PNG said the policy would not work unless women had more say over family size. The ABC said it had sought comment from the government.
keyFacts: Policy is still a proposal
Population growing by over 180,000 a year
Fertility rate of 3.6 births per woman

articles.title: Bupa GP clinic email urged doctors to lift revenue through higher-paying Medicare items
articles.summary:
An email from a Bupa-owned GP clinic told doctors to ensure revenue was increasing and encouraged more chronic condition management plans, which pay $160.60 compared with $87.10 for a standard consultation, the ABC reported. The ABC obtained the email, sent in June.

Bupa said the email was a reminder to consider preventive care and that patient needs always came first, according to the ABC. Royal Australian College of General Practitioners president Michael Wright said GPs should not be pressured over billing. The Department of Health is spending $147 million over four years on Medicare compliance.
keyFacts: Email sent at one Bupa clinic in June
Chronic care plans pay $160.60
Bupa says patient needs come first

articles.title: Senate paraquat inquiry votes not to hold public hearings
articles.summary:
The Senate rural and regional affairs committee examining the regulator's decision on the weedkiller paraquat will hold no public hearings, the ABC reported. Independent senator David Pocock's motion for hearings was defeated with votes from the major parties, and he alleged industry pressure.

Nationals senator Ross Cadell, the deputy chair, denied industry influence, according to the ABC. Parkinson's Australia criticised the decision and is appealing the Australian Pesticides and Veterinary Medicines Authority's June decision to the Administrative Review Tribunal. The APVMA said it did not accept that industry pressure shaped its decision.
keyFacts: Pocock's motion for hearings defeated
Nationals deny industry influence
Parkinson's Australia appealing APVMA decision

articles.title: Wages rise 1.1 per cent in September quarter, fastest quarterly growth since 2023
articles.summary:
The Wage Price Index rose 1.1 per cent in the September quarter and 3.5 per cent over the year, seasonally adjusted, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Wednesday. The ABS said the quarterly rise was the strongest since the December quarter of 2023.

Annual private sector wage growth was 3.4 per cent and public sector growth 3.9 per cent, according to the ABS. It said the Fair Work Commission's 4.75 per cent increase to award wages was a key driver of private sector growth. The ABC reported the public sector figure reflected pay rises for nurses, midwives and police.
keyFacts: Annual wage growth was 3.4 per cent a year earlier
The peak in this cycle was 4.3 per cent in late 2023
Public sector wages have grown faster than private for seven straight quarters, the ABC reported

articles.title: Albanese arrives in China ahead of talks with Xi at APEC in Shenzhen
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has arrived in China, where he is due to meet President Xi Jinping on Friday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, AAP reported. It will be their fifth formal meeting.

Albanese travelled from Manila, where he attended a Quad leaders' meeting with US President Donald Trump and the leaders of India and Japan. He told reporters he raised the cost-of-living effects of the Iran conflict and said he did not expect any backlash from Beijing, describing the relationship with China as strong. He is also due to hold an annual leaders' meeting with Premier Li Qiang in Beijing.
keyFacts: The Xi meeting is scheduled for Friday
The Quad leaders' meeting in Manila ran for about 90 minutes, AAP said
An Australia-China CEO roundtable is planned in Beijing, the ABC reported

articles.title: Australia sanctions settler leader and construction firm over West Bank settlements
articles.summary:
Foreign Minister Penny Wong has announced sanctions on three individuals and four organisations over illegal settlement activity in the occupied West Bank, AAP reported. It is the first time Australia has targeted a construction company and its head under these measures.

According to AAP, those named include settler leader Daniella Weiss and her organisation Nachala, and Itamar Yehuda Levi and the company Eyal Hari Yehuda Ltd. Wong said the measures responded to a rise in settler attacks recorded by the UN, and urged Israel not to proceed with planned settlement building, the ABC reported. Wong said she had spoken to her Israeli counterpart about the sanctions.
keyFacts: Three individuals and four organisations were sanctioned
Breaches carry penalties of up to 10 years' jail, the ABC reported
The UK announced sanctions on Israeli construction firms a day earlier

articles.title: Kuwait says it intercepted drones; US official confirms strike on Qeshm launch site
articles.summary:
Kuwait's army said explosions heard on Tuesday were its air defences intercepting hostile drones, without saying where they came from, Al Jazeera reported. A US official said a US strike had hit a missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm island.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they used drones against a US-operated radar at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa air base, citing what they called repeated violations of Iranian airspace. Bahrain said the attack was intercepted, and US Central Command said there was no damage, according to Al Jazeera. An Iranian deputy governor told IRNA residential and commercial areas on Qeshm were not damaged.
keyFacts: Kuwait did not name the source of the drones
The US confirmation follows Iranian reports of attacks on Qeshm
Iran said more tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday

articles.title: Ukraine partly destroys Crimea bridge after second strike in two days
articles.summary:
Ukraine has partly destroyed the 19-kilometre bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea after striking it twice in two days, AAP reported, citing Reuters. Earlier reports on Monday said traffic had been restricted and the Kremlin had described the damage as minor.

Crimea's Russian-installed governor, Sergei Aksyonov, said two people were killed, according to the report. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said a repair plan would be drawn up. President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Russia strikes Ukrainian infrastructure, including bridges, every day. The bridge was opened by Vladimir Putin in 2018.
keyFacts: What changed: the bridge is now reported partly destroyed after a second strike
Two people were killed, according to Crimea's Russian-installed governor
The bridge is about 19 kilometres long

articles.title: Israel's new parliament elects speaker backed by Netanyahu's opponents
articles.summary:
Israel's newly elected parliament has chosen a Knesset speaker backed by the bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot, replacing Amir Ohana, an ally of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, CNN and the ABC reported. Israel Hayom reported earlier that the bloc had agreed to nominate Matan Kahana for the post.

CNN said the vote weakened Netanyahu's hold on parliament while coalition negotiations continue after the election. The speaker controls the parliamentary agenda, including the timing of votes. Netanyahu has called for a unity government with Eisenkot, citing the threat from Iran.
keyFacts: Amir Ohana held the speakership in the previous Knesset
No new government has yet been formed
The speaker sets the Knesset's agenda

articles.title: Nvidia beats revenue forecasts as chair rules out reinstating Huang
articles.summary:
Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of US$115.8 billion, up 103 per cent on a year earlier, and forecast about US$130 billion for the current quarter, the company said. Analysts had expected a fourth-quarter forecast of about US$125 billion, AAP reported.

What changed: chair Harvey Jones said on the earnings call that the board had unanimously accepted Jensen Huang's resignation and did not intend to reinstate him, according to AAP. Huang had said he would be honoured to return. Interim chief executive Colette Kress is running the company while a recruitment firm searches for a permanent leader.
keyFacts: Data centre revenue was US$107.6 billion
The forecast excludes data centre sales to China
Huang resigned last week

articles.title: WA agrees with Commonwealth on permanent carve-out from gas reservation scheme
articles.summary:
WA Premier Roger Cook said his government had agreed with the Commonwealth on changes to the planned national gas reservation scheme that would permanently exempt Western Australia, NCA NewsWire reported. The changes would need to pass the Senate.

The scheme would require gas exporters to reserve up to 20 per cent of supply for the domestic market. Labor is negotiating with the Coalition on its passage. Opposition resources spokeswoman Susan McDonald criticised the draft legislation and listed the WA carve-out among four Coalition concerns, according to the report. WA already has its own domestic gas reservation policy.
keyFacts: The carve-out needs Senate approval
Exporters would reserve up to 20 per cent of gas
The Coalition has raised four concerns with the bill

articles.title: UK sanctions eight Israeli construction firms over West Bank settlements
articles.summary:
The UK has imposed asset freezes on eight Israeli construction companies over settlement building in the occupied West Bank, Al Jazeera reported, citing Reuters. Firms named include Har Hevron Development Company, Hemdat Shomron and SAG (Velvel) Construction and Development.

The UK also sanctioned the settler group Tzav 9, which it said repeatedly blocked aid trucks bound for Gaza. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told companies not to bid for or build settlement projects, according to the report. The measures came shortly before final tender deadlines for the E1 settlement project east of Jerusalem.
keyFacts: Eight construction firms face asset freezes
Settler group Tzav 9 was also sanctioned
Israel's caretaker government is due to decide on E1 this week, the ABC reported

articles.title: One Nation proposes cutting refugee intake to 2,000 and scrapping parent visas
articles.summary:
One Nation has released a policy that would cut Australia's annual refugee intake from 20,000 to 2,000 and end permanent visas for migrants' parents, AAP reported. Leader Pauline Hanson told reporters in Canberra the lower figure was the limit and denied the plan targeted Muslim-majority countries.

About 150,000 people are in the queue for parent visas, according to AAP. Foreign Minister Penny Wong called the policy harsh and divisive. Shadow treasurer Tim Wilson said One Nation could not be trusted to deliver an immigration policy.
keyFacts: Current annual refugee intake is 20,000
About 150,000 people are waiting for parent visas
The policy was released on Wednesday

articles.title: NSA's classified internal network goes down; agency blames routine maintenance
articles.summary:
The US National Security Agency's classified internal network, NSA Net, went offline on Tuesday, CBS News reported, citing multiple US officials. The agency staggered arrival times at its Fort Meade headquarters and shifted some work to other sites.

An NSA spokesperson said the network suffered temporary degradation during scheduled maintenance and that mission-critical capabilities remained operational, according to Al Jazeera. CBS said officials had seen no evidence of a cyberattack. President Donald Trump told reporters such things happen. The outage followed a Federal Aviation Administration ground stop and a Microsoft outage in recent days.
keyFacts: The network is known internally as NSA Net
Officials said there was no sign of a cyberattack
How long the outage lasted was not reported

articles.title: ASX 200 falls for fifth straight day as banks and miners decline
articles.summary:
The S&P/ASX 200 fell 61.4 points, or 0.69 per cent, to 8,821.8 on Wednesday, its fifth consecutive loss, AAP reported. The All Ordinaries fell 64.9 points, or 0.72 per cent, to 8,932.4.

Ten of the 11 sectors closed lower, led by financials and materials, while energy rose as coal miners recovered, according to AAP. The report linked the fall to stronger than expected wage figures, which it said left open the possibility of another Reserve Bank rate rise. The ABC reported Lendlease shares fell sharply after a broker downgrade.
keyFacts: ASX 200 closed at 8,821.8
Ten of 11 sectors fell
Energy was the only sector to rise

articles.title: Queensland government votes down bill to let abuse survivors sue institutions
articles.summary:
The Queensland government has voted down a private member's bill that would have allowed abuse survivors to sue institutions such as churches and sporting clubs, AAP reported. The bill was introduced by shadow attorney-general Meaghan Scanlon.

Scanlon said the decision showed the government's support for victims was lip service, according to AAP. A Slater and Gordon lawyer said Victoria, the ACT and Western Australia had already closed the legal gap the bill targeted. AAP said it sought comment from Attorney-General Deb Frecklington and did not report a response.
keyFacts: The bill was a Labor private member's bill
It targeted claims against unincorporated institutions
Three other jurisdictions have made similar changes, a lawyer said

articles.title: Israel sends tanks into central Gaza in first ground push since ceasefire
articles.summary:
Israeli forces began a ground operation in central Gaza on Wednesday beyond the so-called Yellow Line, according to Al Jazeera and Euronews. The military said it was targeting Hamas infrastructure and acting to remove a threat to its troops. Tanks were reported east of Nuseirat camp and north of Bureij, and families fled parts of Nuseirat.

Hospital officials said three Palestinians were killed in the operation, Al Jazeera reported. Hamas called it a clear violation of the ceasefire. COGAT told aid groups to stay out of the area. An AFP tally based on Gaza health ministry figures puts deaths since the October 2025 ceasefire above 1,600; Israel says seven soldiers have been killed in that time.
keyFacts: It is the first Israeli ground push since the ceasefire began
Hospital officials reported three people killed
Israel says it controls more than 60 per cent of Gaza

articles.title: Democrat Mary Peltola defeats Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska, AP reports
articles.summary:
Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated two-term Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska, according to AP. It was the last US Senate race of the 2026 midterms to be decided. AP said the result gives Democrats a 56-44 majority in the Senate after they flipped nine Republican-held seats.

Peltola said voters had sent a message that the status quo in Washington was not working for Alaska. AP said Sullivan's spokesperson did not respond to a request for comment. A federal judge dismissed a Justice Department lawsuit over the race, and the department has appealed, AP reported. Peltola led Sullivan 49.5 per cent to 41.4 per cent in the August primary.
keyFacts: Alaska was the last undecided Senate race
Democrats will hold 56 of 100 Senate seats, AP said
The Justice Department is appealing the dismissal of its lawsuit

articles.title: Trump arrives in Shenzhen and plans separate meeting with Putin
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen for the APEC summit, where Chinese President Xi Jinping greeted him at the airport, Euronews reported. A first three-way meeting between Trump, Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin is scheduled for Thursday.

A US official told AP that Trump also plans a separate meeting with Putin on Thursday, their first talks since last year's Alaska summit; the timing was unclear. Trump said the joint meeting would cover limiting nuclear weapons and ending the war in Ukraine, AP reported. Trump also said he was very close to a deal on Ukraine and would not raise Taiwan himself, according to Euronews. Putin told a business forum that sanctions and tariffs had outlived their usefulness.
keyFacts: The trilateral meeting is set for Thursday
A US official told AP of a separate Trump-Putin meeting
It would be their first talks since Alaska last year

articles.title: Xi tells APEC business forum China will cut tariffs and widen market access
articles.summary:
Chinese President Xi Jinping told business leaders at the APEC summit in Shenzhen that China supports free and open trade, according to Al Jazeera. He criticised unilateralism and protectionism, without naming the United States.

Xi said China would lower tariffs and expand market access in manufacturing and services, and would offer global companies a more stable and predictable environment, Al Jazeera reported. He said the World Trade Organization should remain at the centre of the trading system. An analyst quoted by Al Jazeera noted Xi did not mention US export controls or Nvidia. The speech came before Xi's meetings with US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
keyFacts: Xi spoke at the APEC CEO summit in Shenzhen
He pledged lower tariffs and wider market access
He said the WTO should stay central to world trade
