articles.title: House Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries as Speaker for new Congress
articles.summary:
House Democrats have nominated Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker in a closed-door vote of 251 to 11, NPR and Al Jazeera reported. Jeffries ran unopposed. If elected by the full House on 3 January, he would be the first Black Speaker of the House.

Al Jazeera said seven of the 11 members who voted against him were newly elected Democrats who cited unmet commitments on issues including Medicare for All and Gaza. NPR reported Democrats are set to control at least 257 seats in the new House. Jeffries said Democrats would deliver change. NPR said some Democrats have publicly questioned whether Chuck Schumer should remain Senate leader.
keyFacts: The caucus vote was 251 to 11
The full House votes on 3 January
Democrats are set to hold at least 257 House seats, NPR said

articles.title: White House withdraws Heidi Overton's nomination to lead the FDA
articles.summary:
The White House has withdrawn Heidi Overton's nomination as commissioner of the US Food and Drug Administration, shortly before a Senate health committee vote, Drug Topics reported, citing The New York Times. Two people familiar with the decision said the White House concluded she lacked the votes, as she needed every Republican on the committee.

Committee chair Bill Cassidy disputed that, saying on social media he believed she would have advanced and that she had been abandoned. Overton was the third person put forward for the role since Marty Makary left in May. Her role in an August executive order on splitting the MMR vaccine had drawn scrutiny. It is unclear who will be nominated next.
keyFacts: The withdrawal came before a scheduled committee vote
Senator Cassidy said she would have advanced
She was the third pick since Makary's May departure

articles.title: Fed minutes show nearly all officials expect a rate rise in December
articles.summary:
Minutes of the US Federal Reserve's 27–28 October meeting show nearly all officials expected to raise interest rates by a quarter point in December, AP reported. Some officials supported a rise in October, and governors Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented in favour of a higher rate.

The Fed held its benchmark rate at 3.9 per cent in October after raising it in September. AP said futures markets put the chance of a December rise near 95 per cent. Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC he backed a half-point rise, while New York Fed president John Williams argued against a move that large, according to AP.
keyFacts: The minutes cover the 27–28 October meeting
Two governors dissented in favour of a rise
Markets priced a December rise at about 95 per cent, AP said

articles.title: UK inflation rises to 3.6 per cent in October as fuel prices climb
articles.summary:
UK consumer prices rose 3.6 per cent in the year to October, up from 3.5 per cent in September, the Office for National Statistics said. The CPIH measure, which includes owner-occupier housing costs, rose 3.7 per cent.

The ONS said transport, particularly motor fuel, made the largest upward contribution. Fuel prices were 33.2 per cent higher than a year earlier, the biggest annual rise since July 2022. Average diesel reached 199.5p a litre, the highest since records began in 1996. Core inflation, which excludes energy, food, alcohol and tobacco, was 2.8 per cent. Restaurants and hotels made the largest downward contribution.
keyFacts: Annual CPI inflation was 3.6 per cent
Motor fuel prices rose 33.2 per cent over the year
Core inflation was 2.8 per cent

articles.title: Hegseth says US and Venezuela have signed deal to restore military ties
articles.summary:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said during a visit to Caracas that the United States and Venezuela had signed an agreement to re-establish military ties, covering areas from training to intelligence sharing, AP reported. The Pentagon did not release further details.

Hegseth described Venezuela as a compliant security partner since US forces captured Nicolás Maduro in January and praised cooperation with interim President Delcy Rodríguez, according to AP. Rodríguez said she hoped cooperation would reach the highest possible level. AP noted that her court-sanctioned term expired in July, she remains head of state, and no date has been set for a presidential election.
keyFacts: The agreement covers training and intelligence sharing
The Pentagon gave no further details
No date is set for Venezuela's next presidential election

articles.title: Anthropic set to debut on Nasdaq after share sale of up to $US90 billion
articles.summary:
AI company Anthropic is due to begin trading on Nasdaq on Thursday US time under the ticker ANT, CBS News reported. Its filing offers 825 million shares at $US70 to $US78, which would raise up to about $US64 billion, plus about $US26 billion from a private placement involving companies including Nvidia and Google.

City AM reported orders reached almost seven times the shares available and that pricing was expected on Wednesday evening, with bankers reportedly guiding to the top of the range. The expected valuation is about $US1.4 trillion. City AM said the company had an annualised revenue run rate of $US81 billion at the end of October and an operating loss of $US567 million in the September quarter.
keyFacts: The offer covers 825 million shares
The price range is $US70 to $US78
The expected valuation is about $US1.4 trillion

articles.title: Sudan's army advances in Kordofan as UN reports most civilian deaths from drones
articles.summary:
Sudan's army has captured the town of Al Khuway and advanced to within about 60km of the RSF-held city of Al Nuhud in West Kordofan, The National reported, citing the conflict monitor ACLED. ACLED said the army and allies had retaken more than 30 towns and villages since early November.

A UN report said more than 1,630 civilians were killed in drone strikes from January to October, about 73 per cent of 2,230 verified civilian deaths, according to The National. Kordofan accounted for more than two-thirds of casualties. A lawyers' group said an army air strike killed at least 13 people in Abu Qalb. Aid groups say the war has killed at least 59,000 people since April 2023.
keyFacts: Drone strikes caused about 73 per cent of verified civilian deaths, the UN said
The army is about 60km from Al Nuhud
A lawyers' group blamed an army air strike for 13 deaths

articles.title: Amnesty says RSF drone strikes on El Obeid should be investigated as war crimes
articles.summary:
Amnesty International said drone strikes by Sudan's Rapid Support Forces on El Obeid in North Kordofan should be investigated as war crimes. It said it examined nine strikes between June and August that killed 37 civilians and injured 10, including attacks on a power plant, fuel stations and the main market.

Amnesty said it found no military targets near the sites. Secretary-General Agnès Callamard called for the Darfur arms embargo to be extended across Sudan and to cover drones. Amnesty said the RSF replied in October denying responsibility and blaming the Sudanese army, without providing evidence. The RSF and the army have been at war since April 2023.
keyFacts: Amnesty examined nine strikes from June to August
It said 37 civilians were killed
The RSF denied responsibility, Amnesty said

articles.title: Telstra outage drives 72 per cent rise in outage complaints to telco ombudsman
articles.summary:
More than 13,000 Australians lodged complaints with the Telecommunications Industry Ombudsman in the September quarter, the ABC reported. A 12-hour Telstra outage on 8 July drove a 72 per cent rise in complaints that mentioned outages.

Telcos paid $1.9 million in compensation to 2,267 people who complained, according to the ABC. FTI Consulting estimated the Telstra outage cost the economy $552 million. Consumer group ACCAN said the figures understated the problem and called for automatic compensation. Ombudsman Cynthia Gebert urged telcos to act quickly and fairly. Telstra said 99 per cent of complaints made directly to it had been resolved.
keyFacts: More than 13,000 complaints were lodged in the quarter
Outage-related complaints rose 72 per cent
Telcos paid $1.9 million in compensation

articles.title: Whistleblower alleges Canberra patients removed from surgery lists to cut wait times
articles.summary:
Independent ACT MLA Thomas Emerson told the Legislative Assembly that a whistleblower alleged Canberra Health Services clerks were told to remove elective surgery patients who had waited more than 500 days, without consulting doctors, the ABC reported. The alleged aim was to improve average wait-time figures, and staff who refused were allegedly threatened.

Canberra Health Services chief executive Janet Zagari called the allegations extremely disturbing and said no policy allowed removal without clinical review, according to the ABC. The service will commission an independent audit. Health Minister Marisa Paterson said the allegations were being treated with the utmost seriousness. The claims have not been tested.
keyFacts: The allegations were raised during annual report hearings
They concern patients waiting more than 500 days
An independent audit will be commissioned

articles.title: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth, 49 years after launch
articles.summary:
NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft was due to reach one light-day from Earth on 18 November, about 26 billion kilometres away, according to NASA and Space.com. At that distance a radio signal takes 24 hours to travel each way, so a command and its reply take two days.

Space.com said the milestone was expected at 10:16 GMT, or 9:16pm AEDT. Voyager 1 launched in September 1977 and in 2012 became the first human-made spacecraft to enter interstellar space, NASA said. It travels at about 61,000km/h. Its twin, Voyager 2, is expected to reach the same distance in November 2035, according to Space.com.
keyFacts: One light-day is about 26 billion kilometres
Signals take 24 hours each way
Voyager 2 is expected to reach the mark in 2035

articles.title: Woolworths plans 100 to 125 new supermarkets over five years
articles.summary:
Woolworths plans to open 20 to 25 new stores a year over the next three to five years, adding 100 to 125 supermarkets over five years, AAP reported. The company opened 127 stores in the past decade.

Chief executive Amanda Bardwell told an investor briefing on Wednesday that new stores support the company's online growth, according to AAP. About two-thirds of its 1,130 Australian supermarkets have been renewed, and 60 to 85 more will be refitted each year. AAP said scan-and-go trolleys are in 100 stores, with a wider rollout planned before Christmas.
keyFacts: Woolworths has 1,130 Australian supermarkets
It plans 20 to 25 openings a year
It opened 127 stores in the past decade

articles.title: Wife of Melbourne activist held in Vietnam urges stronger push for his release
articles.summary:
The wife of Melbourne activist Tran Hiep, who has been detained in Vietnam since September, has urged the federal government to press harder for his release, AAP reported. Vietnamese authorities say he is accused of terrorism and forging documents; he was taken from Cambodia.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese raised the case with Vietnam's prime minister at the ASEAN summit on Sunday, according to AAP. Chloe Dang welcomed that but said her husband's case should not be treated like criminal cases. His lawyer said normal diplomacy was not working. Vietnamese authorities said detained men admitted membership of Viet Tan, which Vietnam lists as a terrorist group. A consular visit is set for 20 November.
keyFacts: Tran Hiep, 51, is held in Ho Chi Minh City
Albanese raised the case at the ASEAN summit
A consular visit is scheduled for 20 November

articles.title: Rubio says no evidence recent US outages were caused by a hostile actor
articles.summary:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was zero evidence that recent outages affecting Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration, JPMorgan Chase and the National Security Agency were linked or caused by rival countries or criminals, AP reported.

The outages have disrupted US flights, business services and the NSA's classified internal network in recent days. The NSA has attributed its outage to routine maintenance, and Microsoft said its outage was caused by an earlier network capacity upgrade. Rubio made the comments while travelling with President Donald Trump in Asia, according to AP.
keyFacts: Rubio cited outages at four organisations
He said there was no sign of a malign actor
The NSA blamed its outage on maintenance

leftOut.title: ABC wins scoop of the year at 71st Walkley Awards
leftOut.summary:
The ABC won seven awards at the 71st Walkley Awards for journalism, held in Sydney on Thursday night across 30 categories, the ABC reported. Scoop of the Year went to an ABC Investigations team for reporting on what ASIO knew before the Bondi attack.

Other ABC winners included Foreign Correspondent's Gaza Children of War in the international category and Four Corners' Brutal Force in current affairs, according to the ABC. Walkley Foundation chief executive Shona Martyn said public interest journalism was in good hands. Other outlets' winners were not detailed in the ABC report.
keyFacts: 71st Walkley Awards held in Sydney
ABC won seven of 30 categories
Scoop of the Year for Bondi ASIO reporting

leftOut.title: Port Adelaide takes Dougie Cochrane at No.1 in AFL draft
leftOut.summary:
Port Adelaide selected Dougie Cochrane with the first pick of the AFL national draft after matching an Essendon bid, AAP reported. Essendon took Ethan Drevers at No.2 and Carlton took father-son prospect Cody Walker at No.3.

Sydney took Brisbane academy player Caylen Murray at pick nine after Brisbane fell three points short of the draft value needed to match the bid, AAP said. Nineteen players were picked on the first night at Marvel Stadium, including five Indigenous players in the first round. The draft resumes on Friday night.
keyFacts: Cochrane taken at pick one
19 players picked on opening night
Draft resumes Friday night

leftOut.title: Caitlin Foord named AFC international women's player of the year
leftOut.summary:
Matildas and Arsenal striker Caitlin Foord was named the Asian Football Confederation's international women's player of the year at a ceremony in Bangkok, AAP reported. She previously won the AFC youth award in 2011 and the women's player award in 2016.

Foord is the second Australian to win the international award, after Ellie Carpenter in 2024, AAP said. She has 152 caps and 42 goals. Iranian goalkeeper Alireza Beiranvand won the men's player award, the first goalkeeper to do so, and North Korea's Kim Kyong-yong won the women's award.
keyFacts: Awards held in Bangkok
Foord has 152 caps and 42 goals
Beiranvand first goalkeeper to win men's award

leftOut.title: Melbourne walk against family violence to begin 16 days of activism
leftOut.summary:
The 18th annual Walk Against Family Violence is scheduled in Melbourne on Friday, starting at 10am from Birrarung Marr, AAP reported. Organisers say it marks the start of 16 days of activism against gender-based violence and coincides with Transgender Day of Remembrance.

AAP spoke with survivors and advocates taking part, including a woman who now works with perpetrators of family violence. The report listed support services including 1800 RESPECT. No new government policy was announced in connection with the event.
keyFacts: 18th annual walk held in Melbourne
Marks start of 16 days of activism
Starts at Birrarung Marr at 10am

leftOut.title: Economists put recession risk higher after rise in unemployment
leftOut.summary:
Economists said the rise in unemployment to 4.9 per cent in October increased the risk of an Australian recession, AAP reported. AMP chief economist Shane Oliver put the risk at about 40 per cent and cited five Reserve Bank rate rises in 2026.

Independent economist Saul Eslake said unemployment could reach the RBA's 5 per cent forecast as early as 2027, AAP said. He said a recession indicator known as the Sahm rule could be triggered in early 2027 if unemployment keeps rising at its recent pace. October inflation figures are due on Wednesday.
keyFacts: Unemployment rose to 4.9 per cent in October
Oliver puts recession risk near 40 per cent
October inflation data due Wednesday

leftOut.title: Businesses seek wider China market access before Albanese meets Xi
leftOut.summary:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is due to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on Friday before travelling to Beijing for talks with Premier Li Qiang, the ABC reported. Executives from companies including BHP, Rio Tinto and ANZ are due to meet Chinese counterparts in Beijing.

The Business Council of Australia is seeking greater access for beef, rice, medical technology, resources and agricultural technology, according to the ABC. Business Council president Geoff Culbert is expected to say business confidence depends on trust and predictability. No outcomes from the meeting have been announced.
keyFacts: Albanese due to meet Xi on Friday
Talks with Li Qiang to follow in Beijing
Business Council seeks wider market access

leftOut.title: Elton John urges government to protect Australian artists from AI
leftOut.summary:
Singer Elton John used a recorded address to the ARIA Awards to urge the federal government to protect Australian artists and their work from artificial intelligence, the ABC reported. The government is consulting on changes to copyright law.

Acting Prime Minister Richard Marles told News24 he understood the concern and that creative workers should be fully compensated, according to the ABC. The government has not announced the outcome of its copyright consultation. The ACTU separately welcomed recently announced mandatory AI guardrails, the ABC reported.
keyFacts: Message delivered at the ARIA Awards
Government is consulting on copyright changes
Marles said creators should be compensated

leftOut.title: Ukrainian drones reported to hit oil pumping station in Tatarstan
leftOut.summary:
Ukrainian drones struck the Kaleykino oil pumping station near Almetyevsk in Russia's Tatarstan republic overnight, the Kyiv Independent reported, citing a Ukrainian monitoring channel and eyewitness accounts of a fire. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian officials had confirmed the strike in the report.

The Kyiv Independent also cited Reuters reporting that Ukrainian attacks over 20 days had disrupted or halted operations at 15 of Russia's 35 major refineries, according to two industry sources. Ukraine's General Staff confirmed separate strikes on two refineries in Krasnodar Krai earlier in the week.
keyFacts: Strike reported by a Telegram monitoring channel
Not confirmed by officials on either side
Site is about 380km north of Kazakhstan

leftOut.title: Marles defends Albanese's appearance in APEC photo with Putin
leftOut.summary:
Acting Prime Minister Richard Marles said Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's appearance in the APEC leaders' photo with Russian President Vladimir Putin was part of respecting the host, the ABC and SBS reported. Marles said Australia's position on Ukraine could not be clearer.

Albanese said he would respect the wishes of the host and make Australia's position on Ukraine clear, according to SBS. Greens leader David Shoebridge called for tougher sanctions on Russia and an end to Russian oil imports, the ABC reported. Criticism of the photo was reported on Wednesday.
keyFacts: Photo taken at a leaders' banquet in Shenzhen
Marles said it reflected respect for the host
Greens called for tougher Russia sanctions

leftOut.title: Marles restates plan to keep four defence heritage sites in public hands
leftOut.summary:
Defence Minister Richard Marles said four of the 67 defence sites earmarked for sale, including Victoria Barracks in Sydney and Melbourne, Fort Queenscliff and RAAF Williams Point Cook, would be retained and moved to the finance department, the ABC reported. Marles said the government could not afford to maintain unused bases.

The decision to keep the four sites was announced by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese on 8 November, Defence Connect reported. Opposition Leader Angus Taylor said the Coalition had forced the change and would keep campaigning to save other sites.
keyFacts: Four of 67 sites will be retained
Sites move from Defence to Finance
Decision first announced on 8 November

leftOut.title: Former NSW Liberal MP Rory Amon found guilty of sexually assaulting 13-year-old
leftOut.summary:
A NSW Supreme Court jury found former Pittwater MP Rory Amon guilty of the sexual assault and indecent assault of a 13-year-old boy in 2017, the ABC reported. The jury deliberated for about four hours.

The court heard Amon met the boy through a dating app. Amon had argued he believed the boy was 17. He remains on bail, and sentencing is listed for later this month. At an earlier trial in March, Amon was acquitted of most charges and the jury could not agree on two counts.

The offences occurred in 2017
Sentencing is listed for later this month

leftOut.title: Cummins rejects Khawaja's claim that whole team knew of 2018 ball-tampering plan
leftOut.summary:
Australian Test captain Pat Cummins rejected former teammate Usman Khawaja's claim, made in his memoir, that the entire team knew of the 2018 Cape Town ball-tampering plan, the ABC reported. Cummins said he did not know sandpaper was being used.

Cummins said Khawaja had been careless with people's reputations and that legal advice suggested some claims could be defamatory, though he would not take action. He also said the bans given to three players were too harsh. Cricket Australia has ruled out reopening its investigation.
keyFacts: The comments came at a press conference in Sydney
Cricket Australia will not reopen its investigation
Cummins said he would not sue

leftOut.title: Victoria Police will not charge four Sydney Swans players, citing insufficient evidence
leftOut.summary:
Victoria Police said it would not lay criminal charges against Sydney Swans players Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, James Jordon and Nick Blakey over an alleged incident at a Melbourne hotel in August, citing insufficient evidence after legal advice, the ABC reported.

Police noted an ongoing civil matter and declined further comment. Swans chief executive Matthew Pavlich said the players could now move forward, and the club said it stood by its decision to stand them down. Lawyers for three women are pursuing civil claims.
keyFacts: Police cited insufficient evidence
The alleged incident occurred in August
Civil claims are continuing

leftOut.title: Prosecutors oppose bail for Darwin teenager charged with terrorism offence
leftOut.summary:
A Darwin teenage girl charged with collecting or making documents likely to facilitate terrorist acts appeared in court on Friday, AAP reported. Prosecutor Hadi Mazloum alleged her diary named a student she wanted dead and that she shared a plan to shoot at a school, and argued the risk to the community was too high for bail.

Her lawyer cited significant psychological circumstances and sought a supervised community-based order. The judge adjourned the bail application to Monday. A 14-year-old boy was arrested with her on 3 November.
keyFacts: She was arrested on 3 November

Bail will be decided on Monday

leftOut.title: ABC reports US has held talks with Myanmar's military-backed government over rare earths
leftOut.summary:
The Trump administration has held talks with Myanmar's military-backed government ahead of the ASEAN summit in the Philippines, the ABC reported, citing a State Department document that lists countering China and access to rare earth resources among the goals.

The talks followed the detention of a former American Chamber of Commerce head at Yangon airport in June. A Lowy Institute analyst described it as hostage diplomacy, and a human rights advocate criticised the talks. The US has previously accused Myanmar's military of genocide.
keyFacts: China controls about 90 per cent of rare earth output, an analyst said
The ASEAN summit is in the Philippines

leftOut.title: 1960 paper had predicted population would become infinite on 13 November 2026
leftOut.summary:
A 1960 paper in the journal Science predicted world population would approach infinity on 13 November 2026, based on a formula drawn from historical fertility and death rates, the ABC reported. The date was chosen to fall on lead author Heinz von Foerster's birthday.

An economist quoted said the projections held until about the 1980s. Global population growth peaked at about 2.3 per cent a year in 1963, and the UN projects population will peak at just over 10 billion in about 60 years.

Growth peaked in 1963
The UN projects a peak just over 10 billion

leftOut.title: Olympic cyclist Rohan Dennis admits breaching good behaviour bond
leftOut.summary:
Olympic medallist Rohan Dennis admitted in the South Australian District Court that he breached a good behaviour bond, AAP reported. The bond, imposed in 2025 over the December 2023 crash that killed his wife Melissa Hoskins, carries a suspended 17-month jail term.

Dennis was caught driving while disqualified in June, with two children in the car. Judge Emily Telfer ordered a supervision compliance report and adjourned the matter to 1 February.

The bond carries a 17-month term
The matter returns on 1 February

leftOut.title: Man dies in workplace incident in Adelaide's north-east
leftOut.summary:
A 26-year-old man died at the scene of a workplace incident on Leopold Street, Vista, in Adelaide's north-eastern suburbs on Friday, South Australia Police said, according to the ABC. Emergency services were called at about 12.15pm.

SafeWork SA said it had been notified and sent an investigator and an inspector. SA Power Networks workers were seen examining a power pole nearby. Police will prepare a report for the coroner. No cause has been stated.
keyFacts: The man was 26
SafeWork SA is investigating
A report will go to the coroner

leftOut.title: CBA and NAB chiefs to face parliamentary hearings after fee and wage cases
leftOut.summary:
Commonwealth Bank chief Matt Comyn and NAB chief Andrew Irvine were due to appear before parliamentary hearings on Friday, AAP reported, after NAB agreed to repay $169 million to 66,000 underpaid staff and ASIC began proceedings against CBA over $8.5 million in undisclosed business fees.

Committee chair Ed Husic, a Labor MP, criticised NAB's plans to move about 180 roles offshore. Westpac's chief disclosed a 28 per cent gender pay gap at the hearings.
keyFacts: Hearings continued on Friday
NAB is repaying $169 million
ASIC is suing CBA over $8.5 million in fees

leftOut.title: Ottawa agency weighs artificially freezing part of Rideau Canal skateway
leftOut.summary:
Canada's National Capital Commission is considering refrigerating a 900-metre stretch of the Rideau Canal in downtown Ottawa so it can be used for skating more often, The Canadian Press reported. The commission's chief operating officer, Tobi Nussbaum, told CBC News that a feasibility study proposed using refrigeration pipes.

Nussbaum said the number of skating days could triple, but not before 2030. The canal opened for only 10 days in 2024 and did not open to skaters in 2023, according to The Canadian Press. The study links the shorter seasons to warmer winters.
keyFacts: Stretch under study is 900 metres long
Skating days could triple, the commission says
Not expected before 2030

leftOut.title: Republicans acknowledge midterm defeat but few call for a break with Trump
leftOut.summary:
Republican lawmakers have acknowledged that voters rejected them in the midterm elections but have shown little interest in breaking with President Donald Trump, AP reported. Representative Richard Hudson, who led the House Republican campaign arm, said voters felt costs were too high. House Speaker Mike Johnson said voters made the wrong choice.

Senator Josh Hawley blamed cuts to rural healthcare, and Representative Lauren Boebert said the party had collectively failed, according to AP. Democrats flipped more than 40 Republican-held House seats. The piece is an analysis of reactions rather than a report of a new event.

Hudson led the House Republican campaign arm
Analysis piece drawing on lawmakers' comments

leftOut.title: US travel restrictions keep some African contestants out of Miss Universe
leftOut.summary:
Some contestants from African countries may miss the Miss Universe pageant in Puerto Rico on 24 November because of visa problems linked to US travel restrictions, The Daily Beast reported. Miss Universe Zambia organisers said their contestant, Pamela Mubanga, had been forced to withdraw.

Zimbabwe's Roseanna Hall said her visa approval had stalled, and South Sudan's Amylia Deng said her participation was uncertain, according to The Daily Beast. The restrictions on nationals of a number of countries took effect on 1 January 2026. The outlet said it had sought comment from the State Department.

Zambia's contestant has withdrawn
Restrictions took effect on 1 January 2026

leftOut.summary:

The allegations are separate from a joint ITV and Guardian investigation published earlier in the week.

Walliams denies the allegations and says he has not broken the law. Detective Superintendent Mike Cagney is leading the inquiry. Police have not said how many offences were reported or when they allegedly occurred.

Walliams denies any wrongdoing

leftOut.summary:

Brand was convicted last week of rape and three counts of sexual assault and was sentenced on 9 November to 10 years and six months in prison, NME reported. He has previously denied wrongdoing. London police are investigating two further rape allegations.

leftOut.summary:

Coach Tony Popovic made several changes and gave debuts to four players: Eli Adams, Sam Klein, Kasey Bos and Diesel Herrington, according to AAP. Australia had 14 shots to Qatar's three. The Socceroos play Jordan in Doha on Tuesday, Wednesday Australian time.

leftOut.summary:
California Governor Gavin Newsom said he would decide in early January whether to run for president in 2028, the Sacramento Bee and Fox News reported. He made the comments to Turkey's Anadolu Agency at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya.

Newsom, who leaves office in January, has previously said he would consult his family first and would not run if former vice-president Kamala Harris entered the race. Harris has not commented publicly, according to the Sacramento Bee. Newsom said the recent midterm results would factor into his decision.

Green linked the move to the recent failed attempt to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth. In September the House voted 232 to 147 to set aside an earlier Green impeachment resolution. The report did not include a response from the White House or House leaders.

September resolution set aside 232-147

leftOut.summary:
President Donald Trump posted support on Truth Social for a bipartisan bill offering federal incentives for film and television production while a nationwide FAA ground stop was in place on Friday, TheWrap reported. It said he had not publicly addressed the flight disruption at that time.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy had posted that a communication issue was behind the stoppage and that technicians were investigating, according to TheWrap. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the cause was not yet known but it was not a terrorist attack.

leftOut.title: Albanese and Bowen caught on open microphone joking at COP31
leftOut.summary:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen were recorded on an open microphone sharing a private joke at the COP31 climate summit in Türkiye, the ABC reported in a short video. The remark involved a crude reference.

The exchange came as Albanese left the summit for the ASEAN meeting in Manila, while Bowen stays on to lead negotiations, according to AAP. Neither minister had commented on the recording in the ABC's report.

ABC published a short video
No comment from either minister reported

leftOut.title: Australian aid workers recall 2001 detention by Taliban, 25 years on
leftOut.summary:
Two Australians held by the Taliban in 2001, Peter Bunch and Diana Thomas, have described their detention and rescue to AAP, 25 years after it ended. They were among eight Shelter Now International staff arrested in Kabul in August 2001 and accused of promoting Christianity.

After US strikes began and Northern Alliance forces advanced, the group was freed from a jail in Ghazni and later flown out by US special forces, reaching Pakistan on 15 November 2001, AAP reported. Former prime minister John Howard told AAP it was a dramatic time.

leftOut.title: Gunman's daughter gives evidence at Perth double murder inquest
leftOut.summary:
The daughter of Mark Bombara, who shot dead Jennifer Petelczyc and her daughter Gretl at their Perth home in May 2024, gave evidence at the WA Coroners Court on Friday, AAP reported. Bombara, who had been looking for his estranged wife, then killed himself.

Ariel Bombara apologised to the victims' family and called for change on family and domestic violence, according to AAP. She criticised police for allowing her father to keep 13 firearms despite warnings. The acting state coroner will deliver findings at a later date.

Findings to be delivered later

leftOut.summary:
The Greens want parliament to end the lower excise rate on fuel used by private aircraft, with leader David Shoebridge citing Parliamentary Budget Office costings, AAP reported. The PBO estimated the change would raise $640 million in 2027 and $1.5 billion over the forward estimates.

Shoebridge said motorists pay 53.7 cents a litre in fuel tax compared with about 3.6 cents for jet owners, according to AAP. He named several high-profile jet owners as beneficiaries. The government's response was not included in the AAP report.

leftOut.title: Insurers receive more than 2,700 claims after storms in Queensland and NSW
leftOut.summary:
Insurers have received more than 2,700 claims after supercell storms hit south-east Queensland and northern NSW on Wednesday, the Insurance Council of Australia said, according to AAP. About 2,400 claims came from Queensland, and about 300 related to food spoiled during power cuts.

About 25,000 homes lost power on Thursday, and the SES received more than 300 calls, most in Logan, AAP reported. The Bureau of Meteorology warned of further storms and possible flash flooding over the weekend. Insurance Council chief Andrew Hall urged policyholders to keep receipts.

leftOut.title: Data show more small businesses raising prices after card surcharge ban
leftOut.summary:
A growing share of small businesses that previously added card surcharges have raised prices since the ban took effect on 1 October, according to payments company Tyro, AAP reported. Tyro's Nigel Lee said the share rose from 9.4 per cent in the first week to 12.4 per cent three weeks later.

Of those businesses, 61 per cent lifted prices by more than the old surcharge, Lee said. He expected more increases before the end of the year as rent, power, wage and interest costs rise. The ban is expected to save consumers about $1 billion over time.

The surcharge ban began on 1 October

leftOut.title: National working with children check database expands as SA joins
leftOut.summary:
A national system that tracks criminal records of Working With Children Check holders in near real time is expanding, with South Australia joining from Monday, AAP reported. The pilot already covers Commonwealth and ACT offences, but full coverage across all jurisdictions is not expected until 2028.

Attorney-General Michelle Rowland blamed differences between state systems for the timeline and said the government wanted to beat it. The 2015 royal commission into institutional child sexual abuse recommended a central database. The federal government has invested $37 million, and all jurisdictions have confirmed they will join.

States must opt in, with no deadline
The report was published before this update window

leftOut.title: Equifax data point to rising business exits as David Jones closes stores
leftOut.summary:
Business exits rose 41.3 per cent year on year in the September quarter while new business entries fell more than 15 per cent, according to Equifax data reported by AAP alongside the David Jones collapse. Active tax defaults rose 25 per cent, the data showed.

Equifax's Brad Walters said smaller operators were borrowing to cover immediate overheads. David Jones entered administration and receivership on 5 November and plans to close 19 of its 38 stores. Retail groups forecast $7.2 billion in Black Friday and pre-Christmas spending.

leftOut.title: Man who escaped custody at Melbourne funeral arrested in far north Queensland

Orijol Rukaj, 47, who escaped Corrections Victoria supervision during a visit to a Melbourne cemetery for his brother's funeral in April, has been arrested in Bamaga in far north Queensland, AAP reported. He had been on remand on drug importation charges.

Victoria Police said he would be extradited to Victoria within days, according to AAP. Police did not say how he travelled interstate. Officers have identified several overseas-based people they believe helped him escape. He has not yet faced the original charges in court.

Republican congressman Thomas Massie told Fox News Digital that a new resolution to limit President Donald Trump's military action against Iran could reach the House floor within the next few legislative days or around Christmas. It would be the fourth such attempt this year.

Republican Tom Barrett, who backed an earlier resolution, said he doubted more Republicans would join, according to Fox News, while Republican Jeff Van Drew said one or two might. Armed Services chair Mike Rogers will oppose it. No vote has been scheduled.

An FBI analysis of his phone allegedly found about 88 images, Fox News said, citing court documents. The allegations have not been tested in court. Responses from Brennan's lawyer, the Justice Department and the FBI were not included in the report.

leftOut.summary:
The Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission has voted to cut the East Coast menhaden catch limit by 9 per cent in 2027 and 17 per cent in 2028, adopting a compromise proposed by Maine, according to the Maine Monitor and the Associated Press. The limit falls from 186,840 tonnes in 2026 to 155,000 tonnes in 2028.

The commission also cut the Chesapeake Bay harvest cap by about a third, the Baltimore Banner reported. More than 48,000 public comments were received, most favouring a deeper cut. Fishing industry groups opposed the cap, while conservation groups said it did not go far enough.

leftOut.title: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to limit judges' power to void rules nationwide
leftOut.summary:
The US Justice Department has asked the Supreme Court to restrict courts' power under the Administrative Procedure Act to set aside federal rules for everyone rather than only for the parties to a case, Reuters reported in an analysis. The appeal stems from a challenge by Texas medical providers to federal surprise-billing rules.

The administration argues relief should be limited to plaintiffs, while Republican-led states including Texas and Florida say the law is a key check on federal overreach, according to Reuters. The court is expected to decide early next year whether to hear the case.

leftOut.summary:
Everyone aboard the American Heritage river cruise boat was accounted for after a tanker struck it on the Mississippi River near the Port of New Orleans on Friday, city officials said, according to ABC News in the US. Officials said nearly 200 people were aboard.

About 30 passengers and two crew who ended up in the water were taken to hospital with non-critical injuries, ABC News reported. Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham said the tanker appeared to have lost steering. The National Transportation Safety Board sent investigators, and part of the river was closed.

Authorities advise people to leave beaches and water when thunder is heard. leftOut.summary:

leftOut.summary:
Independent federal MP Helen Haines has been discharged from The Alfred hospital in Melbourne, ABC News reported on Monday. Dr Haines lost both legs after being struck by a car outside her Wangaratta electorate office on 19 October.

Politicians from across parliament welcomed the news, according to the ABC's live coverage. A 43-year-old man, Brendan Nugent, has been charged over the incident, the ABC reported. The charges have not been tested in court. Details of Dr Haines's return to parliamentary duties were not reported in the coverage reviewed.
keyFacts: Helen Haines discharged from The Alfred hospital
She lost both legs after being hit by a car on 19 October
A 43-year-old man has been charged

leftOut.title: Ecuadorian fishers who survived US drone strike plan lawsuit against US government
leftOut.summary:
Sixteen Ecuadorian fishers who say they survived a US military drone strike on their boat in March are suing the US government, Common Dreams reported. They are represented by lawyer Dan Kovalik in the US District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania, according to the report.

The fishers allege the strike on the vessel La Negra Francesca Duarte II was unlawful and that they were later detained in El Salvador, and seek unspecified damages, Common Dreams said. It cited The Guardian as reporting the filing was due on Monday US time. The US government's response was not reported, and the filing had not been confirmed.
keyFacts: 16 fishers say a US drone strike sank their boat in March
Suit to be lodged in the Western District of Pennsylvania
Filing had not been confirmed at the time of reporting

leftOut.title: India warns Bay of Bengal system could become severe cyclone by 17 November
leftOut.summary:
The India Meteorological Department said a depression over the Bay of Bengal was likely to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by 17 November and move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, Business Today reported. A landfall point had not been forecast.

Odisha's disaster management minister Suresh Pujari put all districts on alert, according to the report, after two earlier cyclones in recent weeks. Fishermen were told to return to shore by 16 November, and rain is expected on 18 and 19 November. No damage or casualties had been reported, as the storm had not yet formed.
keyFacts: IMD expects a severe cyclonic storm by 17 November
Odisha placed all districts on alert
Fishermen told to return to shore

leftOut.title: Iran rejects German demand to halt uranium enrichment
leftOut.summary:
Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei rejected a German call for Tehran to stop enriching uranium, citing Iran's rights under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, the Associated Press reported. He also criticised the International Atomic Energy Agency over speculation about a new facility near Isfahan.

Mr Baghaei said the IAEA had lost access during the war with the US and Israel, and that Iran would respond to any attack, according to AP. Germany has said Iran must halt enrichment to ease tensions. The comments repeat Iran's long-stated position on enrichment, and no new nuclear talks were announced.
keyFacts: Iran rejects Germany's call to halt enrichment
Spokesman cites Iran's rights under the NPT
Criticised IAEA over Isfahan speculation

leftOut.title: Hundreds of thousands protest in Prague against public media funding overhaul
leftOut.summary:
A crowd estimated by Czech media at 350,000 to 400,000 gathered at Letná in Prague on Sunday to oppose government plans to change how public television and radio are funded, Euronews reported. The rally was organised by Million Moments for Democracy.

The government of Prime Minister Andrej Babiš wants to replace household licence fees with funding from the state budget. Critics say this would expose the broadcasters to political influence. Radek Vondráček of the governing ANO party described the organisers as professional agitators. The bill passed its first reading in October. Police reported no disturbances.
keyFacts: Crowd estimated at 350,000 to 400,000
Plan would replace licence fees with state budget funding
Bill passed first reading in October

leftOut.title: Estonia to close Russian border crossings after alleged GRU-linked arson attempt
leftOut.summary:
Estonia will close its border crossings with Russia from 1 December after an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems near Tallinn, The Irish Times and Defense News reported. Eight people were detained; officials said the suspects were Latvian citizens.

The head of Estonia's security police, Margo Palloson, said the attack was carried out at the behest of Russian military intelligence. The company said production was not disrupted. Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova called the accusations part of a wave of Russophobia. Estonian authorities did not say how long the closure would last.
keyFacts: Crossings to close from 1 December
Eight detained over attempted attack on Threod Systems
Russia rejects the accusations

leftOut.title: Ecuador's president denies the US has a military base at Taura airbase
leftOut.summary:
Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa said US personnel at the Taura air base near Guayaquil were there only for temporary activities under bilateral cooperation, and that it was an Ecuadorian base, AFP reported. He was responding to an AFP investigation.

AFP reported about 20 US military flights at the base between June and mid-October, along with tents and construction work. Ecuadorian voters rejected allowing foreign military bases in a November 2025 referendum. The Pentagon, US Southern Command and Ecuador's air force did not respond to requests for comment, according to Al Jazeera.
keyFacts: Noboa says US activities at Taura are temporary
AFP counted about 20 US military flights since June
Voters rejected foreign bases in a 2025 referendum

leftOut.title: Megaspeed says alleged spy Alice Huang left the company in 2025
leftOut.summary:
Singapore cloud company Megaspeed said Alice Huang left the company effective 30 August 2025 and holds no current role, AP reported via ABC News. The company said media claims about it were not supported by verifiable evidence and that it had hired outside lawyers for an internal investigation.

US authorities are examining alleged transfers of Nvidia chips to China through the company; Beijing has called such claims unsubstantiated. US Attorney-General Todd Blanche said the Justice Department had not concluded whether Ms Huang is a Chinese spy. Singapore said its own investigation found insufficient evidence of a crime.
keyFacts: Megaspeed says Huang left in August 2025
Company has begun an internal investigation
US says no conclusion yet on spying allegation

leftOut.title: Iranian embassy posts threat naming two US Navy officers
leftOut.summary:
Iran's embassy in South Africa posted a message on X saying 'we will find you' alongside images of the commanding officer and executive officer of the destroyer USS Spruance, Fox News and The Express reported. The ship returned to San Diego after a 357-day deployment that included combat against Iranian forces.

An earlier embassy post had accused the officers of ordering missile strikes that it said killed children at a school in Minab, a claim not independently established. A Foundation for Defense of Democracies analyst said the threat should concern US officials. The US Navy's response was not reported.
keyFacts: Embassy post names USS Spruance's two senior officers
Ship returned after a 357-day deployment
Iran links the officers to a strike on a Minab school

leftOut.title: Pentagon explores prosecuting fired general accused of leaking, Washington Post reports
leftOut.summary:
The Trump administration has directed the US military to explore a criminal case against Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia, the Joint Staff's former top planner, who has been accused of leaking classified information, The Washington Post reported, according to Newsmax. A US official said the matter was referred to the acting Army secretary.

No charges had been laid as of Sunday. Axios previously reported, citing an internal Pentagon report, that General Sylvia admitted leaking information to reporters. People familiar with the case told the Post he denied disclosing classified material. Military law experts said a court-martial would require a preliminary hearing.
keyFacts: Matter referred to the acting Army secretary
No charges laid as of Sunday
General reportedly denies disclosing classified material

leftOut.title: Trump calls ABC reporter 'pathetic' over question on White House renovation spending
leftOut.summary:
US President Donald Trump called ABC News reporter Rachel Scott 'pathetic' after she asked about spending on renovations in Washington while the air traffic control system needed funding, The Independent reported. Mr Trump said the White House renovations cost 'peanuts'.

The Independent cited Justice Department filings showing the ballroom cost estimate had risen from $US200 million to as much as $US600 million. Mr Trump has blamed ageing equipment and the Biden administration for Friday's nationwide flight ground stop. The Independent said total renovation projects across the capital exceed $US1.65 billion in public money.
keyFacts: Trump says renovation costs are 'peanuts'
Ballroom estimate has risen to as much as $US600 million
Exchange followed Friday's FAA ground stop

leftOut.title: Trump administration presses Congress for $US50 billion to overhaul air traffic control
leftOut.summary:
The Trump administration is seeking $US50 billion to overhaul the US air traffic control system, AP reported. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said he would send a detailed request to legislators on Monday, but had not specified how the money would be spent.

Congress approved $US12.5 billion in 2025, and the FAA administrator has said at least another $US10 billion is needed for a second phase, according to AP. The FAA has said Friday's nationwide ground stop was caused by a router overload during contractor work. Democrats are seeking answers about earlier spending.
keyFacts: Administration seeks $US50 billion
Congress approved $US12.5 billion in 2025
FAA blames router overload for Friday's ground stop

leftOut.title: Washington teen sentenced to probation over shooting that injured boy at recreation centre
leftOut.summary:
A 19-year-old Washington man who pleaded guilty to aggravated assault and carrying a pistol without a licence was sentenced to probation over a May shooting that injured a boy playing basketball, the US Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia said. Prosecutors had sought five years.

Judge Jennifer Di Toro imposed a suspended 24-month sentence with 18 months of supervised probation under the Youth Rehabilitation Act, over the government's objection, according to the office. Fox 5 DC reported the man fired more than 20 rounds. A search of his home found two firearms, prosecutors said.
keyFacts: Prosecutors sought five years in prison
Judge imposed suspended sentence and probation
More than 20 rounds were fired, prosecutors say

leftOut.title: Darwin girl, 15, granted bail on terrorism document charge
leftOut.summary:
A 15-year-old Darwin girl charged with collecting or making documents likely to facilitate terrorist acts was granted bail in the Northern Territory Youth Justice Court on Monday, AAP reported. She was arrested on 3 November and cannot be identified.

Judge Greg Macdonald found exceptional circumstances, citing her age, mental health and family support, according to AAP. Conditions include no internet-capable devices, adult supervision and the removal of guns from the home. Allegations raised at the hearing have not been tested. A 14-year-old boy faces related charges, and the case returns to court on 15 December.
keyFacts: Charge carries a maximum of 15 years
Bail granted with strict conditions
Case returns to court on 15 December

leftOut.title: Elderly driver who killed boy in Canberra car park avoids jail
leftOut.summary:
An 81-year-old woman who pleaded guilty to culpable driving causing the death of a four-year-old boy in a Canberra shopping centre car park received a suspended sentence of two years and three months, ABC News reported. Her licence was suspended indefinitely.

ACT Supreme Court Justice Belinda Baker said the woman was not intoxicated or speeding and did not realise the car was still in drive. Prosecutors had argued for full-time custody. The boy's parents had asked for the lightest possible sentence and said afterwards the result was fair, according to the ABC.
keyFacts: Suspended sentence of two years and three months
Licence suspended indefinitely
Prosecutors had sought full-time custody

leftOut.title: Robert Irwin named Queensland's 2027 Australian of the Year
leftOut.summary:
Conservationist Robert Irwin, 22, has been named Queensland's 2027 Australian of the Year for his environmental advocacy and work at Australia Zoo, ABC News reported. Sprinter Gout Gout, 18, was named Young Australian of the Year for Queensland.

Disability advocate Carmel Crouch, 80, was named the state's Senior Australian of the Year, and Cairns Hospital greeter Noel Brown received the Local Hero award, according to the ABC. National Australia Day Council chief executive Carrie Leeson congratulated the recipients.
keyFacts: Robert Irwin named Queensland Australian of the Year
Gout Gout named Young Australian of the Year for Queensland
Carmel Crouch named Senior Australian of the Year for Queensland

leftOut.title: Albanese says he will raise Iran war concerns at Quad meeting with Trump
leftOut.summary:
Anthony Albanese said he would raise Australia's concerns about the Iran war when he meets Donald Trump and the leaders of India and Japan in Manila on Tuesday evening, AAP reported. It is the first Quad leaders' meeting since 2024.

Protests led by left-wing groups, students and workers have been held in Manila for four days against Trump's attendance, according to AAP. Albanese said he had a good relationship with Trump and that Australia wanted de-escalation. The meeting had not taken place at the time of this update.
keyFacts: Quad leaders due to meet in Manila on Tuesday evening
First Quad leaders' meeting since 2024
Protests in Manila against Trump's attendance

leftOut.title: Zelenskiy says Ukraine, US and European officials agreed to meet in Berlin
leftOut.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Monday's online talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and European officials were difficult, and that participants agreed to meet in Berlin with the coalition of countries backing Ukraine, Al Jazeera and Reuters reported.

Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Russia had not agreed to widen talks beyond existing delegations and no date was set for a next round, according to the report. Kushner said Washington was making progress. Kyiv's mayor said preliminary reports indicated two bridges over the Dnipro were hit.
keyFacts: Online talks held on Monday with US envoys
Participants agreed to meet in Berlin, Zelenskiy said
Kremlin says no date set for next round

leftOut.title: CNN reports US intelligence suggests Iran drew up options for attack in Washington
leftOut.summary:
CNN reported, citing multiple US officials, that new US intelligence suggests Iran has drawn up plans that could target senior Trump administration figures in Washington with a radiological or chemical device, according to the Times of Israel.

The sources said the intelligence does not point to an imminent attack and describes options rather than operations, the report said. One source doubted Iran had the personnel to carry them out, and officials were divided on the intelligence's credibility. Iran has not responded in the reports, and the claims are attributed to anonymous officials.
keyFacts: Report cites anonymous US officials
Intelligence does not indicate imminent attack, sources say
Officials divided on credibility

leftOut.title: Senate Republicans move to fill top US audit office post in lame-duck session
leftOut.summary:
Senate Homeland Security Committee chairman Rand Paul has moved to speed up the selection of the next comptroller general, who heads the Government Accountability Office, Nextgov and Federal News Network reported. A nomination hearing has been scheduled for next week, though the White House had not publicly named a nominee.

Top congressional Democrats said the selection commission had not interviewed any candidates, according to Federal News Network. Office of Management and Budget deputy director Eric Ueland has reportedly been considered for the post. The position has been filled on an acting basis since Gene Dodaro retired in December 2025.
keyFacts: Nomination hearing scheduled for next week
Democrats say no candidates were interviewed
Eric Ueland reportedly considered for the role

leftOut.title: Victorian party leaders to take part in single town hall debate before election
leftOut.summary:
The leaders of Victoria's four major parties will take part in a town hall-style debate on Tuesday, the only pre-election debate the two major parties agreed to, AAP reported. Victorians vote on 28 November, and there will be no one-on-one debate between Premier Ben Carroll and Opposition Leader Jess Wilson.

Wilson accused Carroll of avoiding a head-to-head, while Carroll said Wilson did not want to share a stage with One Nation, according to AAP. A Monash University political scientist told AAP a debate gaffe would be high risk for the major leaders.
keyFacts: Four-leader town hall debate set for Tuesday
Victorian election is on 28 November
No head-to-head between Carroll and Wilson

leftOut.title: Robert Pattinson announced as the next James Bond
leftOut.summary:
Robert Pattinson, 40, has been announced as the next actor to play James Bond, replacing Daniel Craig, AAP reported. The announcement was made on the official 007 Instagram account, and Pattinson becomes the seventh actor in the role.

Denis Villeneuve will direct the untitled film from a script by Steven Knight, according to AAP. Production is expected in 2027 with release in 2028. It is the first Bond film since Amazon took creative control of the franchise.

Denis Villeneuve to direct
Release expected in 2028

leftOut.title: UK minister criticises Russell Brand's statement from prison
leftOut.summary:
Senior UK minister Ed Miliband described a message Russell Brand issued from prison as disgusting, AAP reported. Brand's wife read the statement, in which he said he was not guilty. He was jailed for 10.5 years for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others.

AAP reported Brand has been moved from HMP Wandsworth to HMP Littlehey, a category C prison. Miliband also said it was time to debate age of consent laws and that he regretted a 2015 interview on Brand's show, according to AAP.

Brand was jailed for 10.5 years
Brand moved to a category C prison, AAP reports

leftOut.title: Mother denies starting fatal Russell Island house fire at coronial inquest
leftOut.summary:
Samantha Stephenson denied starting the August 2023 house fire on Russell Island, south-east of Brisbane, which killed her partner and five children aged three to 11, AAP reported. She was the first witness at a Queensland coronial inquest that began on Monday.

Counsel assisting said the fire likely started on the ground floor and deliberate ignition could not be ruled out, according to AAP. The inquest will also examine smoke alarm compliance and emergency resources on the island, where fire and rescue crews were nearly an hour away by barge. Hearings are set to run for two weeks.

Inquest opened on Monday
Hearings will run for two weeks

leftOut.title: Bowen presents 18-page COP31 draft calling for faster fossil fuel phase-out
leftOut.summary:
Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen, president of the COP31 negotiations, released an 18-page draft agreement in Antalya, Türkiye, the ABC reported. The draft draws on submissions from 160 countries, calls for accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels and seeks 35 per cent electrification of global energy by 2035.

It also proposes tripling adaptation funding to at least $US120 billion by 2035, according to the ABC. Greenpeace described the language as among the strongest in a COP draft. Bowen said not all parties would agree. Critics pointed to Australia's fossil fuel project approvals; Bowen defended exports to countries in transition.
keyFacts: Draft has 144 provisions
Seeks 35 per cent electrification by 2035
Bowen says the text is not final

leftOut.title: Magnitude 6.6 earthquake near Indonesia's Tanimbar Islands felt across NT Top End
leftOut.summary:
A magnitude 6.6 earthquake struck near Indonesia's Tanimbar Islands at about 6.41am Darwin time on Tuesday, the Bureau of Meteorology said, according to the ABC. Geoscience Australia said it began 42 kilometres beneath the Banda Sea.

More than 450 people reported feeling the tremor across the Northern Territory's Top End, including Darwin, Palmerston and Katherine, the ABC reported. Most shaking was weak or light. The bureau said there was no tsunami threat to Australia, and no damage was reported.
keyFacts: Quake was 42km below the Banda Sea
More than 450 felt reports
No tsunami threat to Australia

leftOut.title: Bureau says possible tornado damaged homes at South West Rocks
leftOut.summary:
The Bureau of Meteorology said it was possible a tornado struck South West Rocks on the NSW Mid North Coast at about 4.45pm on Monday, the ABC reported. The bureau was still assessing radar data and reports.

Three homes lost their roofs, and the SES received more than 30 calls for help, according to the ABC. Elsewhere in north-east NSW, 43 millimetres of rain fell in 30 minutes at Grafton and hailstones up to six centimetres were reported at Lawrence.
keyFacts: Three homes lost roofs
SES received more than 30 calls
Bureau still assessing whether it was a tornado

leftOut.title: Inquest hears Perth teen shot by police consumed extremist material
leftOut.summary:
A forensic psychiatrist told the inquest into the death of 16-year-old James Leslie Hollands that he had consumed extremist online content, including beheading videos, the ABC reported. Hollands was shot dead by police at a Willetton Bunnings in May 2024 after stabbing a man.

Dr Natalie Pyszora said there was no sign he was planning a terror attack and that his risk had been assessed as low, according to the ABC. The family's lawyer questioned police leading the countering violent extremism program, while a senior detective supported it.
keyFacts: Inquest into May 2024 police shooting
Psychiatrist saw no sign of attack planning
Family questions police role in program

leftOut.title: Sam Wood takes bail appeal to Queensland Court of Appeal
leftOut.summary:
Fitness personality Sam Wood, charged with assaulting and strangling his wife on the Sunshine Coast in October, has taken his bail application to the Queensland Court of Appeal, the ABC reported. He intends to contest the allegations.

After two unsuccessful bail applications, his lawyers argued a Supreme Court judge's refusal was unreasonable and did not consider whether proposed conditions would reduce risk, according to the ABC. The court heard allegations about an argument in which he is accused of grabbing his wife by the throat.

Two earlier bail bids failed
He intends to contest the charges

leftOut.summary:
Donald Trump was scheduled to sign a trade agreement with Thailand during his visit to Manila for the ASEAN summit, AP reported on Tuesday. Trump has said Thailand will eliminate tariffs on US exports under the deal.

AP did not report details of the agreement or confirm that it had been signed. Trump is in Manila for an ASEAN-US special summit and talks with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr before travelling to China for the APEC meeting in Shenzhen.

leftOut.summary:
Donald Trump said at a state luncheon in Manila that the US had concluded a large trade deal with the Philippines, Reuters reported. He did not give details, and Manila did not announce an agreement.

The office of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr had no immediate comment, according to Reuters. Trump also said Thailand would remove tariffs on US goods under a deal expected in the coming weeks. Marcos said separately that no agreement on the US-led Pax Silica technology initiative would be signed during the visit, The Chronicle reported.

leftOut.summary:
US President Donald Trump is due to hold a three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China on Thursday, Al Jazeera reported. The White House and the Kremlin announced the plan last week, according to The Washington Post.

The meeting is set for the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. No agenda has been published. The talks were first reported several days ago, and no new details were released on Wednesday.

leftOut.title: Ukrainian community group criticises Albanese over summit photo with Lavrov
leftOut.summary:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese appeared alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov in the East Asia Summit family photo in Manila on Tuesday, AAP reported. Kateryna Argyrou, who chairs the Australian Federation of Ukrainian Organisations, told AAP the image was deeply disappointing.

Albanese did not rule out appearing in a photo with Vladimir Putin at APEC in China, according to AAP. In his summit address, he condemned Russia's war against Ukraine as unprovoked and unjustified.

leftOut.title: AUSTRAC chief says some Australians turn a blind eye to money laundering
leftOut.summary:
AUSTRAC chief executive Brendan Thomas said in a Sydney speech that some ordinary business people are helping criminals launder money, AAP reported. He said he was concerned by how willing some members of the public were to ignore financial crime.

Thomas said businesses newly covered by anti-money laundering rules since July had filed more than 1,000 reports, according to AAP. He also pointed to illicit tobacco, crypto ATMs, bookkeepers offering laundering services and scam bots built with artificial intelligence.

Newly regulated businesses have filed more than 1,000 reports
Thomas spoke in Sydney on Wednesday

leftOut.title: Microsoft's Nadella urges Australian firms to treat some AI models as insider risks
leftOut.summary:
Microsoft chief executive Satya Nadella told an AI event in Sydney that businesses adopting artificial intelligence should do so with high ambition, but treat some models as an insider risk, AAP reported. He said much more work was needed on AI safety.

Nadella spoke in a pre-recorded conversation with Commonwealth Bank chief executive Matt Comyn. AAP reported the Australian Cyber Security Centre issued more than 4,400 warnings of potential malicious activity last financial year, up 80 per cent. CBA announced a free cybersecurity tool called CodeCheck.

Cyber warnings rose 80 per cent last financial year

leftOut.title: Undecided voters rate Wilson ahead of Carroll in Victorian leaders' debate
leftOut.summary:
Opposition Leader Jess Wilson was rated best by 39 per cent of 100 undecided voters at Tuesday night's Victorian leaders' debate, AAP reported. Premier Ben Carroll was rated best by 7 per cent, Greens leader Ellen Sandell by 25 per cent and One Nation leader Warren Pickering by 16 per cent.

Wilson and Carroll exchanged remarks about former premiers, according to AAP. A Redbridge survey published in the Australian Financial Review put the Coalition on 31 per cent, Labor 23, One Nation 22 and the Greens 15. Carroll said he was focused on the vote on 28 November.

leftOut.title: Tasmanian premier signals possible cost rise for Hobart AFL stadium
leftOut.summary:
Tasmanian Premier Jeremy Rockliff told parliament it would be no surprise if costs for the Macquarie Point stadium in Hobart increased, AAP reported. The 23,000-seat roofed stadium was last estimated at $1.13 billion, up from an initial budget of $715 million.

Rockliff did not say whether the government would keep its $875 million funding cap or seek parliament's approval for more money, according to AAP. Greens leader Rosalie Woodruff and independent Meg Webb called for transparency. A cost update is due by 23 November.

leftOut.title: Court releases ballistics videos in murder trial of former NSW police officer
leftOut.summary:
The NSW Supreme Court has released police ballistics reconstruction videos from the murder trial of former senior constable Beau Lamarre-Condon, AAP reported. He has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Paddington in February 2024.

The Crown alleges Baird was shot twice and Davies once, according to AAP. Lamarre-Condon says he shot Baird once in self-defence and that the second shot and Davies's death were accidental. Closing submissions are due to begin on Thursday.

leftOut.title: Defence calls Crown case weak in trial of former RAAF pilot accused of murder
leftOut.summary:
Defence barrister Saul Holt KC told a Brisbane jury the prosecution case against former RAAF pilot Robert John Crawford was one of the weakest circumstantial cases a court would see, AAP reported. Crawford is accused of killing his wife Frances at their property west of Brisbane in July 2024 and staging a lawnmower accident.

In his closing address, Holt disputed the Crown's description of the couple's marriage and pointed to a late-night text message from Frances, according to AAP. The Crown is due to begin its closing on Thursday.

leftOut.title: Vet practice apologises after Melbourne Cup runner's remains filmed in skip bin
leftOut.summary:
A veterinary practice has apologised after footage showed the body of Melbourne Cup runner So You Are in a skip bin at a waste facility in Sydney, AAP reported. The horse, which finished eighth in the Cup, was euthanised on Monday after colic.

REC Equine Specialists said it did not carry out the burial but had chosen the provider, and had stopped using it, according to AAP. Trainer Bjorn Baker said he was deeply distressed. Racing NSW said it would take action if its investigation found wrongdoing.

leftOut.summary:

Two acts lead with eight nominations

leftOut.title: England beat Australia by 97 runs in Hobart to win ODI series 2-1
leftOut.summary:
England beat Australia by 97 runs in the third one-day international in Hobart on Wednesday to win the series 2-1, the ABC reported. England had lost the first match in Perth.

leftOut.summary:
English newspapers have criticised Australian Test captain Pat Cummins after claims about the 2018 ball-tampering affair in Usman Khawaja's autobiography, the ABC reported. Columnists in the Daily Mail and The Telegraph said his credibility had been damaged.

Cameron Bancroft, one of three players banned over the affair, published a long article in The West Australian claiming the whole team knew about the sandpaper, according to the ABC. leftOut.title: People with disability call for more accessible music festivals
leftOut.summary:
Music fans with disability say festivals need to do more to include them, the ABC reported ahead of the International Day of People with Disability. A 2022 Creative Australia survey found 40 per cent of people with disability attend festivals, compared with 45 per cent of others.

Rapper MC Wheels said a lack of accessible toilets was a major barrier, according to the ABC. Ability Fest, founded in 2018, was cited as Australia's first inclusive festival. A researcher said exclusion was often created by environments and systems rather than impairment.

ABC political editor David Speers wrote that Donald Trump's meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen is awkward for US allies including Australia. leftOut.title: ABC previews what Trump, Putin and Xi want from Shenzhen meeting
leftOut.summary:
The ABC's China correspondent previewed the first three-way meeting of Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, due on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen. The White House listed nuclear arms control, the wars in Ukraine and Iran, trade and AI as topics.

Analysts quoted were sceptical of concrete outcomes, and no joint press conference or communique is expected, the ABC reported. The New START treaty lapsed in February. A White House spokeswoman said Trump viewed nuclear proliferation as very dangerous, while a Kremlin aide pointed to the meeting's symbolism.
keyFacts: The meeting is the first of its kind
No joint communique is expected
New START lapsed in February

leftOut.title: About 20 isolated Awá people sighted near village in Brazil's Maranhão
leftOut.summary:
Around 20 isolated Awá people were sighted on Monday in the Arariboia Indigenous territory in Brazil's Maranhão state, according to Brazil's Ministry of Indigenous Peoples, AAP reported. The ministry said the information was preliminary.

Survival International said the group asked a government team for yams and took them back into the forest, according to AAP. It estimates about 100 Awá remain uncontacted. Officials activated an emergency response because of disease risk, and Indigenous affairs agency and health staff are in the area.
keyFacts: About 20 people were sighted
Survival estimates about 100 uncontacted Awá
Officials activated an emergency response

leftOut.title: Von der Leyen presses EU states on €45 billion Ukraine loan for 2027
leftOut.summary:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen is seeking support for a €45 billion loan to Ukraine for 2027, backed by joint EU borrowing, Euronews reported. It would be split into €25 billion for military needs and €20 billion for budget support, covering about two-thirds of Kyiv's expected shortfall.

Ukraine would repay only once Russia pays reparations, according to Euronews. The plan needs unanimous backing before next week's EU summit, and Hungary, Slovakia, Czechia and Bulgaria are resisting. The Commission first proposed the loan in late October.
keyFacts: The loan totals €45 billion
€25 billion is for military needs
It needs unanimous support from 27 members

leftOut.title: Crossbench MPs oppose Labor's late changes to electoral funding laws
leftOut.summary:
Special Minister of State Don Farrell tabled late amendments to federal electoral funding laws that take effect on 1 January, AAP and Guardian Australia reported. The government described the changes as technical. The opposition said it would support them.

The amendments would let parties grow investment funds without the interest counting toward donation caps, Guardian Australia reported. Independent MP Kate Chaney called it a major-party stitch-up, and Senator David Pocock said uncapped money could flow to major parties. Farrell said the reforms aim to end a donations arms race. Zoe Daniel and Rex Patrick are challenging the caps in the High Court.
keyFacts: The laws take effect on 1 January 2027
The opposition will support the amendments
A High Court challenge is under way
